Title: DOSH awaits full mitigation plan for fatal Paya Terubong landslide
Article:
GEORGE TOWN: The Department of Occupational Safety and Health (DOSH) is expected to receive the complete mitigation plan for the Taman Seri Rambai landslide in Paya Terubong tomorrow.
State Local Government Committee chairman H'ng Mooi Lye said Penang DOSH was awaiting the full submission and formal application from the developer's civil engineering firm, Aptitude Consulting Engineers Sdn Bhd, which is acting as the project's superintending officer.
"Penang DOSH's investigation and prosecution section had requested an incident report, and the developer's geotechnical engineer, WYA Consulting Engineers Sdn Bhd, submitted it on Nov 5.
"DOSH is now waiting for the civil engineer to present the complete documentation and formal application to execute mitigation and repair works on the collapsed slope.
"The documents and application are expected to be submitted to DOSH tomorrow for further consideration," he said in a statement.
Yesterday, H'ng said
any punitive action
against the developer would depend on the findings of DOSH's ongoing investigation.
The Oct 25 landslide in Taman Seri Rambai, Paya Terubong, claimed the life of 73-year-old Dr Wong Kar Lin when it crashed into his home. His wife and mother-in-law escaped unharmed.
State authorities held the developer and landowner of a nearby condominium and road development liable for the disaster.
Chief Minister Chow Kon Yeow had warned of potential legal fallout as the incident originated on their site.
An inter-agency meeting chaired by H'ng on Nov 2 reviewed the ongoing investigation and mitigation measures. However, the state maintained that it would not determine liability or negligence until DOSH completed its investigation.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: GOF lance corporal fined RM10,000 for possessing controlled poison
Article:
LAHAD DATU: A General Operations Force (GOF) lance corporal was fined RM10,000 by the Sessions Court here today after pleading guilty to possessing 538ml of liquid containing Diphenhydramine, a controlled poison, in January.
Judge Suhailla Selag imposed the fine on Muhammad Azme Zainudin, 27, and ordered him to serve eight months in jail if he fails to pay.
He was charged with possessing 538ml of liquid containing Diphenhydramine along Jalan Fajar at 12.30pm on Jan 31.
The charge was framed under Section 9(1) of the Poisons Act 1952, read together with Section 9(3), and punishable under Section 32(2) of the same Act.
According to the facts of the case, the accused was arrested by the Lahad Datu police headquarters Narcotics Criminal Investigation Division during a raid at 1.24pm that day.
A search of his bag and motorcycle basket uncovered 23 bottles of liquid suspected to be ketum water, with an estimated total volume of 34.5 litres, and six bottles of Dynadryl Syrup containing suspected cough medicine, with an estimated volume of 600ml.
However, laboratory analysis by the Tawau Chemistry Department found no Mitragynine in the 23 bottles, while samples from the six bottles of Dynadryl Syrup contained Diphenhydramine, with a total volume of 538ml.
In mitigation, the unrepresented accused told the court he had been suspended from duty following the case and was the sole breadwinner for his wife and child.
Deputy public prosecutor Shearil Aizad Murnizam urged the court to impose a deterrent sentence, saying it should serve as a lesson to the accused and other public servants, with public interest taking precedence over individual interests.

Title: Macron's Angkor visit highlights France's century-long conservation role
Article:
SIEM REAP: The newly restored West Mebon temple rises from a reservoir at Cambodia's sprawling Angkor archaeological complex, the latest in a century of conservation projects led by former colonial power France.
French President Emmanuel Macron and Cambodian King Norodom Sihamoni will inaugurate the nearly 1,000-year-old temple on the sidelines of a summit of French-speaking nations in Phnom Penh on Nov 15-16.
Conservationists have restored the 16 towers and surrounding walls over the past 14 years, and put the finishing touches on a stone marker at the entrance last week.
The temple is part of the Unesco World Heritage site at Angkor, once the centre of the Khmer Empire, and includes the national treasure Angkor Wat.
It was here that archaeologists unearthed the largest bronze statue ever found in Cambodia, "Reclining Vishnu", which is now touring the world.
The site is steeped in legend.
"In 1936, a villager had a dream in which the Buddha came to him to ask to be freed from the earth, where he was suffocating," French project coordinator Sarah Coudry told AFP.
Excavations had already taken place on the site but when work restarted at the exact spot indicated by the villager, they found the statue of the Hindu god.
Now the temple itself has been restored, in what Coudry said was like assembling "a giant 3D puzzle without a reference model."
Crucial to the work has been the French School of Asian Studies (EFEO), which in 1908, under the supervision of the French government, began clearing, cataloguing and safeguarding archaeological remnants that had been forgotten in the jungle.
The legacy of a near-century of colonial rule is still contested but archaeologist Roland Fletcher of the University of Sydney said France had made a valuable contribution.
EFEO's work has made visible to the world "one of the greatest cultural achievements of humankind", the Briton said.
"I've always joked that if the British had become the colonial administrators of Cambodia, they would have done nothing with Angkor," he said.
- INTERNATIONAL EFFORT -
Near the EFEO centre in nearby Siem Reap city, a "Dancing Shiva" statue nearly touches the ceiling of the warehouse where it awaits a return to its home at Koh Ker, a Khmer heritage site northeast of Angkor.
The centre's director Eric Bourdonneau is inexhaustible as he describes the meticulous work required to reassemble the five-metre, seven-tonne statue.
Looters had smashed the statue into thousands of fragments at several points during the 20th century but it was finally restored to its former glory this year.
Beyond restoration projects, EFEO sees itself as a research institution, with manuscript specialists, language experts and anthropologists.
"We have this distinctive feature... of covering pretty much all fields of knowledge that will allow us to better understand the history and society of Cambodia," Bourdonneau said.
Conservation efforts at Angkor have become international since independence in 1953, with signs noting contributions to various projects from Japan, South Korea, India and China.
But France still has a unique place: more than a century of excavations, inventories and photographs have made EFEO a kind of scientific memory of the ancient Khmer capital.
- KNOWLEDGE TRANSMISSION -
"The French have a great deal of knowledge, above all documentation," said Kim Sothin, deputy director of the Apsara National Authority, the Cambodian government body that oversees the Angkor complex.
"They have studied all the monuments since 1863," the start of the French protectorate.
"If you want to study archaeology or monumental architecture, you also have to study French so you can read all the old documents written by the French," he told AFP in French.
He said Cambodians do not "yet have all the skills" to work alone.
But this is changing.
Cambodian architect Meng Sovanlylin, 32, is among those who have been trained by the French to help preserve and investigate her country's heritage.
"The older generation transfers all the knowledge to us," she said, perched atop precarious scaffolding in the centre of the Bayon temple.
"And then we can learn and practise... and be able to work by ourselves."
Phem Phan, a 65-year-old worker wearing a yellow hard-hat and a faded blue shirt, sees another, more practical advantage to working with the French.
"The salary is decent," he said. "And when we stop working, we have pensions."--AFP

Title: KLCI to remain volatile amid US midterm election spillover [WATCH]
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The benchmark index FTSE Bursa Malaysia KLCI is expected to remain volatile amid geopolitical risks, domestic political uncertainties and inflationary pressures, as a global technology stock sell-off weighs on investor sentiment despite resilient domestic economic fundamentals.
Affin Hwang Investment Bank head of research Loong Chee Wei expects the benchmark index to face continued volatility, with elevated global bond yields and uncertainty surrounding United States policies posing risks to financial markets.
The caution comes after a sharp overnight sell-off on Wall Street spilled over into Asian markets on Friday, amid concerns that the Democratic Party's victory in the US midterm elections could lead to tighter regulatory scrutiny of artificial intelligence (AI) and slow the expansion of data centres.
The Nasdaq fell 5.5 per cent, wiping out about US$3 trillion in market value from S&P 500 companies, while Japan's Nikkei plunged six per cent.
South Korean and Taiwanese benchmark indices also fell more than eight per cent at one point during early trading.
The sell-off was also felt locally, with the KLCI falling as much as 23.53 points, or 1.4 per cent, to 1,612.33 before recovering slightly to 1,613.85 at the noon break on Friday.
Technology stocks recorded the steepest declines among Bursa Malaysia's sectoral indices, reflecting concerns over potentially tighter US regulations on the AI industry.
Loong identified geopolitical developments as a key risk, particularly uncertainty surrounding US government policies on AI and data centres, which could have wider implications for global technology companies and their supply chains.
"This has led to a sharp correction in technology company share prices that have led the global equity market performance this year," he said.
Domestically, investors are also expected to monitor developments ahead of the Melaka state election on November 14.
Nevertheless, Loong said Malaysia's economic and corporate earnings fundamentals remained supportive of the KLCI at current levels, although a sustained rebound would depend on global market sentiment and foreign fund flows.
He described Malaysia as a relative safe haven in the region, citing its position as a net oil and gas exporter, a growing current account surplus supported by services and electrical and electronics (E&E) exports, as well as a strong investment cycle from both foreign and domestic sources.
NON-TECH SECTOR INTEREST?
In contrast, Kenanga Investment Bank head of research Peter Kong expects the benchmark index to edge higher next week, supported by renewed buying interest in non-technology sectors, particularly banking, utilities and healthcare.
"We expect the KLCI to move mildly higher next week," he said, adding that the research house continued to favour technology companies with stronger revenue visibility, including Kelington Group Bhd, UWC Technology Bhd and Frontken Corporation Bhd.
He said sentiment towards technology stocks remained weak amid valuation concerns, although Kenanga did not anticipate a material impact on corporate earnings in 2027 and 2028.
"Data centre related plays however would provide some support as a modest beneficiary on the back of potential slow-down in new approvals in key data centre states in the US," Kong added.
PROJECTIONS TO REMAIN VOLATILE
Affin Hwang has set the highest year-end FBM KLCI target at 1,730 points, followed by Kenanga and MBSB Research at 1,700 points each.
"At this juncture, we view our end-2026 FBM KLCI target of 1,770 points as an optimistic scenario, with a downward bias toward the 1,700-point level," said MBSB Research.
On monetary policy, both Kenanga and Affin Hwang expect Bank Negara Malaysia to raise the overnight policy rate (OPR) by 25 basis points to three per cent in 2027, with Kenanga expecting the adjustment in the first quarter.
Meanwhile, Affin Hwang expects Brent crude oil prices to average between US$80 and US$85 per barrel in 2026 and 2027, while Kenanga said lower crude oil prices would be a key factor in supporting a re-rating of the consumer sector, although prices are expected to remain volatile.
MBSB Research expects Malaysia's economy to grow by 4.6 per cent in 2027, while market consensus points to 6.6 per cent year-on-year earnings growth for FBM KLCI-listed companies.
Overall, while global uncertainties are expected to keep market sentiment cautious, analysts believe Malaysia's resilient economic outlook and positive corporate earnings prospects could provide some stability to the benchmark index in the weeks ahead.

Title: Rapid KL foils second cable theft attempt in a week
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: An attempted theft of earthing cables along the MRT Putrajaya Line was foiled after a man was arrested in an intelligence-led operation by Rapid KL auxiliary police.
Rapid KL said the arrest followed an attempted cable theft on Saturday, which disrupted train services on the line.
Following the incident, auxiliary police and the Putrajaya Line operations team stepped up patrols, surveillance and security checks at identified high-risk locations, including during the Deepavali holiday period.
In a patrol at about 1pm on Nov 8, auxiliary police personnel found several earthing cables believed to have been targeted by thieves near an electrical substation (BSS) close to Jinjang station.
"Checks found that the cables had been cut elsewhere before being left at the substation, believed to be awaiting collection and removal," it said in a statement today.
Rapid KL said surveillance and monitoring continued in the surrounding area, including along the stretch between Jinjang and Metro Prima stations, to track down those involved.
At 11.57pm, a lorry was spotted entering the area and was believed to have been used to transport the cut cables.
However, the lorry driver fled during the raid, while auxiliary police personnel arrested a suspect and handed him over to the police for further action and investigation.
Rapid KL said this was the second arrest involving attempted cable theft within its operational areas in a week.
It warned that cable theft and trespassing onto railway tracks were not only criminal offences but could also endanger those involved, damage critical infrastructure and disrupt public transport services.
It said it would continue working with the authorities and strengthen security measures to protect its assets and ensure reliable train services.

Title: October building material costs – steel drops while sand inches up
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Malaysia's building material market saw mixed movements in October, marked by a sharp drop in steel prices alongside moderate upticks in sand and cement, according to the Statistics Department.
Monthly unit price index for sand rose between 0.3 and 1.8 per cent across selected areas, with Sandakan recording the highest monthly increase, followed by Kuching (0.8 per cent) and Johor (0.5 per cent).
Cement price indices also recorded slight month-on-month gains ranging from 0.1 to 0.4 per cent. Perak led the monthly rise, while Terengganu, Kelantan and Kuching each recorded an increase of 0.3 per cent.
Despite these marginal monthly index adjustments, the nationwide average price of ordinary Portland cement remained unchanged in October at RM25.80 per 50 kg bag.
On an annual basis, however, the cement unit price index climbed between 0.6 and 7.4 per cent across most parts of Peninsular Malaysia, Sabah, and Sarawak compared to October 2025.
The strongest year-on-year increases were posted in the combined region of Selangor, Kuala Lumpur, Melaka and Negeri Sembilan (7.4 per cent), followed by Terengganu, Kelantan and Kuching at 5.7 per cent each.
In contrast, steel prices extended their downward trajectory.
The average per-unit price of steel—comprising mild steel round bars and Mycon 60 high tensile deformed bars—fell 3.0 per cent month-on-month to RM3,327.30 per metric tonne, down from RM3,431.90 per metric tonne in September.
On a month-on-month basis, the unit price index for steel fell between 0.2 and 10.5 per cent across selected regions, with the highest drop in Perak, followed with a 3.6 per cent decline in Terengganu and Kelantan, and a 1.3 per cent slip in Selangor, Kuala Lumpur, Melaka and  Negeri Sembilan.
Year-on-year, steel unit price indices retreated between 0.6 and 8.2 per cent across all surveyed areas nationwide, according to the department. Perak posted the largest annual contraction at 8.2 per cent, followed by Terengganu and Kelantan (-4.8 per cent) and Miri (-4.0 per cent).
Reflecting the broader decline in steel costs, the Building Material Cost Index (BCI) with steel bars showed regional variation.
In the peninsular, the monthly BCI with steel bars decreased between 0.1 and 3.8 per cent across building categories and regions, while in Sabah, Sandakan posted minor increases of 0.1 to 0.2 per cent, while Kota Kinabalu's prices were unchanged compared to in September.
In Sarawak, Sibu recorded slight decreases between 0.1 and 0.4 per cent across all categories of buildings, whereas Kuching and Miri registered slight increases between 0.1 per cent and 0.2 per cent.

Title: Sabah academic calls for transparency in infrastructure spending
Article:
KOTA KINABALU: The Sabah government should adopt a more transparent approach to infrastructure development, particularly in the disclosure of project details and public spending, said an academic.
Universiti Teknologi Sabah senior lecturer Dr Jain Yassin said it was encouraging that the state government continued to prioritise basic infrastructure, particularly water supply and road connectivity.
"These are fundamental necessities that directly affect people's quality of life and the state's economic activities.
"However, beyond the amount of budget allocated for infrastructure, I believe we should pay greater attention to three important aspects: the rate of project completion, the quality and sustainability of infrastructure, and accountability and transparency in public expenditure.
"The Sabah government has to adopt a more transparent approach by publicly disclosing project contractors, contract values, implementation timelines and project progress.
"This should be a shared commitment between the state and federal governments to ensure that public funds are managed responsibly," said Jain, who is also an adviser to the All-Party Parliamentary Group Malaysia-SDG (Sabah region), in an interview with the New Straits Times.
He was commenting on the announcement by Sabah Finance Minister Datuk Seri Masidi Manjun that the state was expected to table
a larger budget next year.
Beyond addressing basic infrastructure gaps, Jain said the state should focus on strengthening its economic capacity, diversifying its economy and developing new engines of growth.
He said Sabah should begin investing in new sources of economic growth.
"For instance, in preparation for Visit Sabah 2027, budget allocations should go beyond tourism promotion and attracting visitors.
"We need to prepare local businesses, Small and Medium Enterprises (SME) and communities to participate in the tourism value chain and capture the economic benefits.
"Similarly, with the Blue Economy already identified as an important development agenda, it is time to translate the planning into actual projects, investment and economic activities that create jobs and generate income for local communities."

Title: Oxford museum returns 39 Naga ancestral remains to India
Article:
OXFORD: An Oxford University museum on Monday returned the remains of 39 people taken during Britain's colonial rule in India to members of its Naga community.
Almost 30 people from the community based in northeastern Nagaland, a mountainous state bordering Myanmar, travelled to Britain for the ceremony, which the museum's director, Laura Van Broekhoven, called a "historic moment."
The handover at the Pitt Rivers Museum came as part of a broader trend among Western museums reassessing how they acquired exhibits from other cultures, particularly human remains, and in some cases returning them.
The Pitt Rivers, an ethnographic museum founded in the 19th century, has already handed back human remains to Indigenous communities in Australia, New Zealand and the United States.
The Oxford museum has more than 6,000 objects representing Naga culture, the largest collection in the world, and is giving back "ancestral human remains", mainly skulls, to the Naga people.
Van Broekhoven hailed it as "a historic moment that will be part of stories told to next generations" in a speech as both sides signed a formal agreement on the handover.
The remains were already "on their way to Heathrow" airport, the museum director said, after overcoming "so much red tape everywhere."
The museum only removed all human remains from display in 2020, much later than most museums, and still has around 2,700 remains in storage, she told AFP.
These "were collected in times that had different ethics, different thinking, which was not unproblematic when we look at it with the eyes of today", she said.
- 'RESPECTFUL REST' -
Housed in a Victorian Gothic building, the museum is a dark atmospheric space with glass cases crammed with objects, many with handwritten labels.
Naga tribal leaders united for the handover and planned to bury the remains together under a joint memorial in a park.
"We shall put them to respectful rest," one of the tribal leaders, Thejao Vihienuo, told AFP.
The 73-year-old, draped in a traditional shawl, also visited with other Nagas last year as part of the lengthy process.
"It's been six years of working alongside each other on a very delicate matter," the museum director said.
The Naga remains were brought to Oxford between 1910 and 1940. Most were collected by two colonial administrators who were anthropologists.
The museum says on its website that items collected during this era were "frequently confiscated during punitive military expeditions, rather than freely given."
While in Oxford, the delegation met descendants of one of the anthropologists.
"The manner in which these human remains were taken away from our land leaves much for us to speculate," said Vihienuo.
"I suspect that nobody would have given the skull of his father or his grandfather as a gift to another person."
The Naga people once practiced headhunting, severing heads of enemies as trophies, but also kept heads of their own chiefs "at the centre of the villages" and one of the remains is a chief's head, said anthropologist Dolly Kikon, a member of Nagaland's Lotha-Naga community.--AFP
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: PH open to exploring new political cooperation after Melaka polls
Article:
MELAKA: Pakatan Harapan will discuss its political direction, including the possibility of exploring new cooperation with other parties, only after the Melaka election.
Acting Melaka PKR chairman Adam Adli Abd Halim said any decision on political cooperation must first be discussed by the PH Presidential Council before it could be regarded as the coalition's official position.
"For now, we are focused on concluding our campaign ahead of polling day. We have seen several recent political developments, including the emergence of new political alignments, and we do not deny that.
"I see this as one of the dynamics that we need to observe.
"At the PH level, in particular, decisions of this nature will be discussed thoroughly by the Presidential Council before we can arrive at a resolution that can serve as the coalition's direction," he told a daily PH press conference at the coalition's main operations room here today.
He was commenting on a statement by Bersatu secretary-general
Datuk Seri Mohamed Azmin Ali
, who had hinted at the possibility of a more open understanding between the party and PH towards the end of the Melaka election campaign, while stressing that Bersatu could not stand alone.
Adam Adli said recent political developments did not necessarily reflect the parties' official positions unless the matters had been discussed and decided by the Presidential Council.
"We know that recent developments have sometimes given an indication of possible moves ahead.
"However, as long as there is no specific decision on the matter and it has not been discussed by the Presidential Council, we cannot regard it as official.
"We acknowledge that PH itself needs to reassess its political direction after this state election, especially with the General Election expected to take place sometime next year. This requires us to formulate appropriate strategies and approaches," he said.
He added that PH's priority at present was to secure victories for its candidates.
"What has been discussed previously goes only as far as that. As polling day approaches, I believe our focus should be on securing victories for PH candidates," he said.

Title: Malaysia's September IPI climbs 6.3pct as manufacturing sales hit RM191bil
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Malaysia's Industrial Production Index (IPI) expanded 6.3 per cent year-on-year in September, driven primarily by strong manufacturing output that propelled the sector's monthly sales value to RM191.1 billion.
According to the latest figures released by the Statistics Department (DOSM), the September headline growth was underpinned by expansions in manufacturing and electricity generation, which offset continued weakness in mining.
The manufacturing output sector advanced 9.4 per cent year-on-year (August 2026: 7.4 per cent), while electricity generation surged 10.7 per cent (August 2026: 9.0 per cent).
Conversely, the mining sector contracted 9.4 per cent (August 2026: -7.4 per cent), dragged down by lower output in crude petroleum and condensate (-11.8 per cent) as well as natural gas (-7.9 per cent).
On a month-on-month comparison, the IPI rose 1.3 per cent (August 2026: 2.6 per cent), supported by a 2.9 per cent expansion in the manufacturing sector.
The growth momentum in manufacturing production was anchored by export-oriented industries, which expanded 10.7 per cent in September compared to 9.1 per cent in August.
This performance was led by the manufacture of computer, electronic, and optical products, which jumped 19.3 per cent, followed by the manufacture of vegetable and animal oils and fats at 7.9 per cent.
Domestic-oriented industries also gathered pace, rising 6.6 per cent year-on-year (August 2026: 3.9 per cent). Growth was lifted by the 10.6 per cent increase in the manufacture of motor vehicles, trailers, and semi-trailers as well as 10.2 per cent for basic metals.
Meanwhile, processed food products production growth saw an increase of 7.5 per cent in September compared with a year ago.
Reflecting the higher factory activity, the capacity utilisation rate of Malaysia's manufacturing industry climbed to 84.9 per cent in September from 84.1 per cent in August.
High plant usage was bolstered by electrical and electronic products at 88.6 per cent, as well as petroleum, chemical, rubber, and plastic products at 81.7 per cent.
The manufacturing sector's sales value in September surged 12.9 per cent year-on-year to RM191.1 billion, accelerating from a 9.9 per cent expansion (RM185.0 billion) recorded in August. Month-on-month, sales value grew by 3.3 per cent.
The sector engaged 2.45 million employees during the month, representing a 1.4 per cent increase from a year earlier. Total salaries and wages paid climbed 4.0 per cent to RM8.7 billion.
As a result, sales value per employee grew 11.3 per cent to RM78,082, while average monthly salaries per employee rose 2.6 per cent to RM3,568.
For the third quarter of 2026 (Q3 2026), the IPI maintained a solid trajectory, advancing 5.3 per cent year-on-year (Q2 2026: 7.7 per cent) and expanding 4.3 per cent quarter-on-quarter.
Growth during the quarter was anchored by manufacturing (7.8 per cent) and electricity (8.3 per cent), which cushioned a 6.7 per cent contraction in mining.
Manufacturing sales value for Q3 2026 grew 10.7 per cent year-on-year to RM553.5 billion (Q2 2026: 9.3 per cent; RM524.8 billion), logging a 5.5 per cent quarter-on-quarter increase.
The sector's quarterly wage bill stood at RM25.8 billion—up 3.4 per cent—with sales value per employee rising 9.1 per cent to RM226,091 and average monthly salaries advancing 2.0 per cent to RM3,517.
Cumulatively, for the first nine months ended September 2026, Malaysia's overall IPI registered a growth of 5.7 per cent, significantly outpacing the 2.9 per cent growth recorded in the corresponding period of 2025.
Over the same nine-month period, manufacturing sales value reached RM1.58 trillion, up 8.5 per cent compared to 3.6 per cent growth in January–September 2025, while total salaries and wages paid reached RM77.4 billion, reflecting an increase of 2.9 per cent.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Recently freed drug offender faces death penalty over heroin trafficking charge
Article:
BATU PAHAT: A man who was recently released after serving a sentence for a drug offence now faces the death penalty after being charged with trafficking 115g of heroin and possessing methamphetamine.
Rahaimi Misnon, 48, an unemployed father of one, nodded as the charges were read out before magistrate Mustaqim Sukarno at the Yong Peng magistrate's court today.
No plea was recorded for the heroin trafficking charge as it falls under the jurisdiction of the High Court.
Rahaimi is accused of trafficking 115g of heroin at the roadside near a house in Jalan Sungai Nibong, Semerah, at 3pm on Nov 3.
The charge was framed under Section 39B(1)(a) of the Dangerous Drugs Act 1952, punishable under Section 39B(2) of the same Act.
Upon conviction, he faces the death penalty or life imprisonment and at least 12 strokes of the rotan if the death penalty is not imposed.
Rahaimi, however, pleaded not guilty to a separate charge of possessing 5.10g of methamphetamine at the same time and place.
The possession charge was framed under Section 12(2) of the Act and is punishable under Section 39A(1).
Deputy public prosecutor Nur Shahzleen Ibrahim prosecuted, while Rahaimi was unrepresented.
The court denied bail and fixed Jan 13 for mention pending the chemistry report.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Three Myanmar children maintain innocence over intimidation charge, out on RM4,000 bail each
Article:
BUKIT MERTAJAM: Three Myanmar children pleaded not guilty at the magistrate's court today to a charge of criminally intimidating an elderly woman.
The three — comprising two 11-year-olds and a 12-year-old — maintained their innocence after the joint charge was read to them in Myanmar by a court-appointed Myanmar interpreter before magistrate Roshayati Radellah.
They were accused of threatening to cause injury to a 71-year-old woman using various objects, including a mop, an iron rod, a fluorescent tube, and stones.
The offence allegedly occurred outside a house in Tingkat Binjai Empat Belas, Taman Sri Rambai about 6pm on Oct 22.
The charge was framed under Section 506 of the Penal Code, read together with Section 34, which provides for up to two years' imprisonment, a fine, or both upon conviction.
During proceedings, their counsel S. Sagthiyaraj, who is representing them pro bono under the Penang Legal Aid Centre, confirmed receiving the relevant documents from Deputy Public Prosecutor Zulfadzli Hassan.
He requested a date for case management, and the magistrate fixed Dec 18.
The three children previously claimed trial to the same charge on Oct 30 when it was read to them in Bahasa Malaysia.
The court had then fixed today's hearing for a Myanmar interpreter to be appointed to explain the charge to them.
Bail was initially denied.
However, speaking to reporters after today's proceedings, Sagthiyaraj said all three children had since been released on RM4,000 bail each following an urgent revision at the High Court.
He said the judicial revision was initiated by the magistrate on Oct 30 after procedural irregularities involving Section 84 of the Child Act 2001 were identified.
The provision stipulates that children charged with non-capital offences cannot be detained on remand and must be released on bail into the custody of their parents or guardians.
Sagthiyaraj said the children, who attend an NGO-run school, had initially struggled to understand the court proceedings due to language barriers and were briefly sent to a moral rehabilitation centre in Air Itam.
"Following swift interventions and concerns raised by non-governmental organisations, the learned magistrate filed an urgent revision before Judicial Commissioner Suraiya Mustafa Kamal at the Butterworth High Court.
"The emergency hearing took place at 5.45pm and concluded at 6.45pm that same day, with the same Deputy Public Prosecutor handling the matter.
"The High Court allowed bail at RM4,000 for each child, with their respective parents acting as sole sureties," he said.
Sagthiyaraj said the children were subsequently brought back to the Bukit Mertajam court complex to complete the necessary documentation and were released at 7.45pm that evening.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: TM expands digital growth across AI, cloud and cybersecurity
Article:
TELEKOM Malaysia (TM) is expanding its capabilities in artificial intelligence (AI), cloud computing, cybersecurity and digital infrastructure as it seeks to translate its technological strengths into stronger business growth.
TM's success in securing awards across four categories at the PIKOM Digital Excellence Awards 2026 reflects its ongoing transformation and growing focus on digital services.
A key part of this transformation has been the application of technology to improve its own operations.
At the core of TM's strategy is a scalable, end-to-end digital ecosystem designed to reduce operational friction and accelerate growth for consumers and businesses.
TM has significantly transformed its Digital Business Support System, streamlining its product portfolio by more than 99 per cent and reducing launch times from months to just three weeks, while maintaining operational stability.
This agile foundation strengthens TM's ability to respond to customer needs more quickly, introduce new services efficiently and deliver integrated Quad Play solutions spanning fixed voice and broadband, mobile and lifestyle services.
The same approach applies to AI
Rather than treating AI as a standalone technology trend, TM has focused on applications that improve customer experience, automate processes and support better decision-making.
Combined with its cloud, data and cybersecurity capabilities, this approach enables AI to be deployed within a secure and well-governed environment.
TM's strength lies in its ability to integrate a broad range of capabilities, from connectivity and cloud computing to cybersecurity, AI and digital platforms.
These capabilities increasingly work together to address customer needs, while partnerships enable the group to draw on additional expertise and solutions where they add value.
This reflects TM's ambition to evolve from a traditional connectivity provider into an orchestrator of a broader digital ecosystem.
Sustainability is also becoming an integral part of this transformation
In 2025, TM's data centre ecosystem avoided more than 190,000MWh of energy consumption and over 149,000 tonnes of carbon dioxide equivalent (tCO2e) in annual emissions through load optimisation and resource sharing.
The group is also applying technology to initiatives such as smart urban forestry and helping micro, small and medium enterprises (MSMEs) adopt practical digital tools.
As Malaysia strengthens its position as a regional digital hub, the challenge is increasingly about translating infrastructure investment into stronger local businesses, deeper digital capabilities, a skilled workforce and long-term economic value.
For TM, the next phase of growth will depend on converting its infrastructure and technological capabilities into greater commercial value, while helping Malaysian businesses and the country capture more opportunities from the digital economy.

Title: EC targets 95 per cent turnout for Melaka early voting
Article:
MELAKA: The Election Commission is targeting a 95 per cent turnout for early voting in the Melaka election today.
Its chairman, Datuk Seri Ramlan Harun, said the turnout stood at 53.225 per cent as at 10.35am, with 5,286 military and police personnel having cast their votes.
He said a total of 9,769 military personnel and 2,792 police personnel were eligible to vote in the early voting today.
"Early voting has begun at 31 polling centres across Melaka, involving 50 streams.
"We hope the trend will continue until this evening and that turnout will reach 95 per cent," he said after inspecting the early voting process at the SK Terendak polling centre here today.
Ramlan said the EC was satisfied with the voting process so far, which had started at all 31 polling centres involving 50 streams statewide.
He said some polling centres would close in stages, depending on the number of registered voters at each stream.
"Nineteen polling centres are scheduled to close at noon, another three about 2pm, while nine will close about 5pm," he said.
In a related development, Ramlan said 237 election offences had been reported to the EC's monitoring team as at last night.
"The reported offences involved matters related to campaigning, flags, campaign materials and other issues. These were minor offences under election regulations," he said.
He added that no major incidents had been reported throughout the campaign so far.
"We have a few more days to go, and I hope this trend will continue.
"I urge all parties to continue campaigning in a responsible and orderly manner without causing any disturbances," he said.

Title: Growing data centre demand for electricity an opportunity for Petronas – Johari
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Petroliam Nasional Bhd (Petronas) could tap new opportunities in the domestic natural gas market as Malaysia's growing data centre industry drives demand for electricity, said Investment, Trade and Industry Minister Datuk Seri Johari Abdul Ghani.
He said the rising electricity requirements of data centres could create another commercially attractive market for natural gas, provided it is supplied at market prices without subsidies.
"In the past, Petronas signed long-term contracts with countries such as Japan to export gas. However, with the growth of data centres, there is an opportunity to supply gas for power generation and sell electricity at retail prices.
"Under long-term export agreements, gas is sold at wholesale prices. But by supplying power to data centres, there is an opportunity to obtain commercial market prices.
"Petronas can embark on this, and still export, sell to the data centres. And data centres will pay you the price," he said in his keynote address at the Bursa Malaysia Sectoral Series: Powering the AI Era.
Johari said the growing electricity demand from data centres could also create opportunities to expand and diversify Malaysia's energy supply, particularly through the integration of solar power with battery energy storage systems (BESS).
He said BESS could play a complementary role in the country's energy distribution system by improving efficiency and managing fluctuations in electricity supply.
"For example, batteries can store electricity when generation exceeds immediate demand and release it when needed," he said.
Johari said meeting the rising demand for electricity presents both challenges and opportunities, particularly in attracting new investments in power generation, energy storage, grid technologies, engineering and domestic supply chains.
He said priority should be given to mobilising capital towards solutions that can support Malaysia's long-term energy requirements.
"Ultimately, Malaysia's ambition is not merely to attract more data-centre investments, but to build the infrastructure necessary for a competitive digital economy.
"This must be achieved without compromising the reliability and affordability of electricity for households and existing industries, or the sustainable management of the country's natural resources," he added.

Title: Four more bodies recovered in Pertak water surge tragedy, three missing
Article:
HULU SELANGOR: Four bodies of victims swept away by a water surge at Lata Jebus, Sungai Luit, Kampung Pertak, were retrieved from the river at 11.15am today, while three others remain missing.
A check at the scene found three bodies trapped along the riverbank near Jambatan Senget, about 950m from Lata Jebus, at 9.20am.
Another body was found at 10.20am near a suspension bridge, about 50m from Jambatan Senget and approximately 1km from the incident site.
All four bodies were taken to the Fire and Rescue Department's forward control post in Kampung Pertak after the recovery operation ended at 11.15am.
The identities of the four victims have yet to be established.
Earlier, a 36-year-old local man was found dead near
Pertak
Bridge at 1.30am today.
The discovery brings the number of victims found to five out of the eight people reported swept away by the strong currents.
The search and rescue (SAR) operation is continuing to locate the remaining three victims.

Title: Two Chinese tourists among three injured in boat collision off Semporna
Article:
SEMPORNA: Three people, including two Chinese tourists, were injured after their tourist boat suffered engine trouble and was rammed by another vessel near Pulau Singamata yesterday.
The incident occurred at 11.12am as the boat, carrying eight Chinese tourists, a skipper and three crew members, was travelling from Seafest Jetty to Pulau Bohey Dulang.
Semporna police chief Superintendent Tan Hiap Wah said the boat had stopped in the waters off Pulau Singamata after its engine became entangled in debris.
He said the vessel was struck from behind by another tourist boat while its crew were trying to remove the debris.
"The collision left two Chinese tourists, a 29-year-old man and a 28-year-old woman, as well as one crew member of the first boat with minor injuries," he said in a statement today.
The first boat sustained damage to its rear section, while the skipper and a crew member of the second boat escaped unhurt. Their vessel was also undamaged.
Tan said police received a report from a 39-year-old local man who worked as a boat operator for a tourism company.
The case is being investigated under Section 280 of the Penal Code for negligent navigation of a vessel and Section 337 for causing hurt through an act endangering the life or personal safety of others.

Title: Too early to discuss cabinet reshuffle, says Anwar
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim today said it was too early to discuss the possibility of a cabinet reshuffle.
This follows speculation over the positions of Finance Minister II Datuk Seri Amir Hamzah Azizan and Transport Minister Anthony Loke, amid the possibility of two vacancies in the cabinet.
Amir Hamzah's term as a Dewan Negara member expires next month. His appointment would need to be extended for him to remain in the cabinet.
Loke, meanwhile, is expected to resign, with his resignation to take effect once former prime minister Datuk Seri Najib Razak arrives at his residence to serve the remainder of his sentence under house arrest.
"It's too early," Anwar said when asked about a cabinet reshuffle.
He was speaking after officiating the International Construction Week and International Building and Construction Exhibition.
Asked about Amir Hamzah's position, Anwar said: "Is that so? He has yet to say so."
Earlier, Utusan Malaysia reported that the unity government was expected to undertake a minor cabinet reshuffle following the possibility of two vacancies.
The report, citing sources, said the developments involved Loke and Amir Hamzah.

Title: Floods forecast in Rompin, Jerantut from tomorrow until Nov 14
Article:
KUANTAN: Floods are forecast to hit Rompin and Jerantut from 1am tomorrow until 11.59pm on Nov 14, according to the National Flood Forecasting and Warning Centre of the Department of Irrigation and Drainage.
In a statement, the centre said flooding could occur in areas along the Rompin and Pahang river basins, particularly low-lying and flood-prone locations.
The forecast was issued following a continuous rain alert at the 'alert' level by the Malaysian Meteorological Department (MetMalaysia) at 8.30am yesterday, as well as DID flood forecasting models.
"In Rompin, areas at risk include low-lying locations within a 5km radius of the Rompin River Basin, covering Kampung Aur, Kampung Meripoh, Kampung Tebu Hitam, Pantai Bernas, Kampung Ayau, Leban Chondong, Kampung Gading and Kampung Sarang Tiong.
"Other areas include low-lying locations within a 5km radius of the Pahang River Basin, covering Kampung Mikang, Kampung Buluh Nipis, Kampung Simpang Sepayang, Kampung Sepayang, Kampung Tebu Hitam, Kampung Tengah, Kampung Tekek, Perumahan Murah Kampung Tekek, Kampung Serinkin, and Kampung Janglau 1, 2 and 3," it said.
In Jerantut, areas at risk include low-lying locations within a 5km radius of the Pahang River Basin, covering Perumahan Felda Jengka 24 in Block 11, Taman Ria, Perumahan Sungai Jan and Felda Gelanggi 1 and 3.
Other locations include Kampung Baharu, Kampung Besul, Kampung Jerangsang, Kampung Sungai Siam, Kampung Lata Kasah, Kampung Kuala Pengau, Kampung Kuala Teh, Kampung Batu Balai, Kampung Sempadan, Felda Sungai Retang, Felda Padang Piol and Kampung Paya Garuk.
"DID will continue to monitor the situation and issue flood warnings if significant rainfall persists in the river basins concerned.
"Flooding may occur earlier or later than forecast.
"All disaster management agencies and residents, particularly those in areas expected to be affected, are advised to remain vigilant and heed instructions from the authorities," it said.

Title: Police probe fireworks display at Jalan Kuala Kangsar junction
Article:
IPOH: Police are investigating a fireworks display at a traffic junction along Jalan Kuala Kangsar after a video of the incident went viral on Threads.
The video shows a group of people setting off fireworks at a traffic light-controlled T-junction, while vehicles pass through the area.
Perak police chief Datuk Mohd Alwi Zainal Abidin said police had yet to receive any reports on the incident.
However, he said police would investigate the incident to identify those involved and establish the circumstances surrounding it.
"We will also check whether there are any closed-circuit television (CCTV) cameras in the surrounding area that could assist in our investigation.
"Police view this matter seriously as such activities could endanger other road users and should not have happened," he told reporters at the Perak Police Contingent Headquarters.
He said celebrations should be held at appropriate venues without disrupting traffic or inconveniencing the public.
"Celebrations should not be carried out in a manner that affects other road users or the general public," he said.
On the legal provisions that could be invoked, Alwi said police had yet to determine the relevant sections.
"We will conduct a thorough investigation first before deciding which section of the law will be applied," he said.

Title: Foreign institution continues buying Malaysian stocks
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Foreign institutional investors extended their net buying streak on Bursa Malaysia to a second consecutive week, recording RM381.3 million in net inflows, according to MBSB Research.
The firm said foreign institutions were net buyers throughout all five trading sessions, signalling sustained foreign interest in the domestic equity market.
Tuesday recorded the highest net foreign inflow at RM152.4 million, followed by Monday at RM102.5 million.
This was followed by Thursday with RM55 million, Friday with RM40.6 million and Wednesday with RM30.8 million.
"The top three sectors with net inflows from foreign institutions were financial services (RM249.5 million), transportation and logistics (RM199.8 million) and construction (RM191.4 million).
"The top three sectors with net foreign outflows were technology (RM221.5 million), plantation (RM126.7 million), and industrial products and services (RM59.8 million)," said MBSB Research in a note.
Meanwhile, local institutional investors extended their net selling streak to a second consecutive week, recording net outflows of RM621 million.
In contrast, local retailers maintained their buying momentum for an 11th consecutive week, registering net inflows of RM239.7 million.
Trading activity also strengthened across all investor categories, with average daily trading volume rising 5.6 per cent among retailers, 17.6 per cent among local institutions and 16.8 per cent among foreign institutions.

Title: China's trade surplus soars past US$1tril as AI boom powers exports
Article:
BEIJING: China's trade surplus surged past US$1 trillion in the first 10 months as a global race to build AI infrastructure buoyed sales of high-tech products and helped offset weak domestic demand, a dynamic likely to sharpen tensions with major trading partners.
The figures highlight Beijing's growing reliance on overseas demand to support an economy hobbled by subdued consumption and a protracted property slump.
But while the global AI investment boom is expected to keep demand for Chinese technology products strong into 2027, it risks deepening domestic imbalances and fuelling trade frictions with partners, including the European Union.
Exports rose sharply by 35.20 per cent in October from the same month last year in US dollar terms, customs data showed on Tuesday, only a touch slower than the 36.30 per cent surge in September, but ahead of economists' forecast for an increase of 33.50 per cent.
That helped lift China's trade surplus to US$1.04 trillion in the first 10 months, topping US$1 trillion for a second consecutive year and reaching the milestone a month earlier than in 2025.
The swelling surplus could fuel further tensions with the European Union, where leaders have called for more trade curbs with China after reaching an agreement with Beijing to limit Chinese exports of hybrid vehicles to the bloc over the next few years.
Because the measures have yet to take effect, factories are expected to bring forward shipments, bolstering exports in the near term.
China on Monday officially announced the extension of a trade truce with Washington due to expire on Nov 10 by two months, but said last week that expanding its purchases of US farm goods would hinge on the implementation of their agreed reciprocal tariff-reduction arrangement.
"The risk of additional tariffs and other trade barriers will remain elevated in 2027, particularly as Chinese manufacturers continue expanding their presence in overseas markets," said Joe Peissel, lead macroeconomist at Trivium China.
Imports grew 41.60 per cent, beating the median forecast for a 32 per cent increase in the Reuters poll and accelerating from the 31 per cent growth in September.
The Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation summit will take place next week in the southern Chinese tech and innovation hub of Shenzhen, where Chinese President Xi Jinping and US President Donald Trump are expected to meet for the third time so far this year.
HEADWINDS AND UNCERTAINTIES
One big worry for Beijing is that consumers remain reluctant to spend, constrained by a property market downturn that has battered household wealth and dented confidence in the economic outlook.
Sluggish demand at home has pushed Chinese automakers to seek sales in overseas markets.
China's car exports maintained a solid pace of growth in October, while domestic vehicle sales recorded a 12th straight month of declines, separate data released by an industry association showed.
Greater reliance on exports, however, leaves China's economy increasingly exposed to any slowdown in global demand.
Much of the strength in exports this year has been fuelled by a global push to expand AI infrastructure.
"The outlook for exports depends on how long the AI boom will last," Macquarie analysts wrote. They expect China's exports to accelerate further in the fourth quarter before starting to slow from the first quarter of 2027.

Title: Melaka polls: EC awaiting full report on website cyberattack
Article:
MELAKA: The Election Commission is investigating claims that its website was targeted in a cyberattack during the Melaka election.
Its chairman, Datuk Seri Ramlan Harun, said the commission had yet to receive a full report on the matter and would issue a statement soon.
"I have yet to receive a full report on the matter. Once we receive it, the EC will issue a statement.
"We hope the cyberattack will not affect our website, as it is crucial to the conduct of the election," he told reporters after inspecting the early voting process at SK Kem Terendak here today.
Ramlan said the EC had been working with the relevant authorities to ensure its systems remained secure against any attempts at intrusion.
"We have been working with all the relevant authorities to ensure this does not happen. God willing," he said.
Asked whether the EC would lodge a report with the Malaysian Communications and Multimedia Commission (MCMC), he said the commission was already working with the relevant agencies.
"We have been working together and are taking steps to protect our systems from being breached," he said.

Title: Switch to defensive stocks as investors move away from manufacturers, tech, says BIMB
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: BIMB Securities Research has adopted a more defensive stance on Malaysian equities, expecting the FTSE Bursa Malaysia KLCI (FBM KLCI) to trade within a narrow range as a global technology sell-off and falling commodity prices weigh on market sentiment.
The firm said the benchmark index was likely to consolidate between 1,610 and 1,630 points, with the 1,600-point psychological level serving as a key support amid heightened external uncertainties.
It said the investment strategy had shifted towards defensive sectors, particularly banking and domestic infrastructure, as institutional investors moved away from export-oriented manufacturers and technology stocks.
"High-conviction institutional rotation has abruptly abandoned export-driven manufacturing champions in favor of defensive financial heavyweights and domestic infrastructure anchors, creating a localised insulation layer to defend the solid 1,600 psychological support baseline against intense post-election global monetary pressure," it said.
BIMB Securities said the shift followed a sharp correction in global technology shares, driven by concerns over tighter artificial intelligence (AI) regulations in the United States following its midterm elections.
The sell-off also spread across Asian markets, with Taiwan's TWSE, South Korea's KOSPI and Japan's Nikkei falling 12.2 per cent, 11.7 per cent and 9.3 per cent respectively last week, reflecting their exposure to the global AI hardware supply chain.
The FBM KLCI closed at 1,616 points, up 0.31 per cent week-on-week last week, but remained down 3.78 per cent year-to-date.
Despite the external volatility, BIMB Securities said foreign investors remained net buyers of Malaysian equities, recording net inflows of RM381 million for the week ended Nov 6.
"The major inflow came into the financial, transportation and construction sectors, with Public Bank attracting RM154.2 million, Westports Holdings RM140.5 million and Malayan Banking RM100.9 million in net foreign purchases," it said in a note.
The firm said the financial sector gained 2.2 per cent week-on-week, supported by its defensive characteristics and Bank Negara Malaysia's decision to maintain the overnight policy rate at 2.75 per cent.
However, the technology and energy sectors were the biggest laggards, declining 9.0 per cent and 6.7 per cent respectively last week as investors reassessed earnings prospects amid the global technology rout and weaker oil prices.
BIMB Securities said the sharp correction in commodities had also changed the outlook for Malaysia's energy and plantation sectors.
Brent crude fell 16.4 per cent to US$98 per barrel, as expectations of a diplomatic de-escalation in the US-Iran conflict reduced geopolitical risk premiums.
Crude palm oil prices also declined 9.0 per cent to RM4,049 per tonne, weighed down by record-high stockpiles and weaker crude oil prices, which reduced the profitability of biofuel production.
In contrast, gold rose 5.1 per cent to US$4,070 an ounce as investors sought safe-haven assets amid economic uncertainty.
The ringgit remained stable at RM4.06 against the US dollar, despite a 0.4 per cent increase in the US dollar index to 102.3.
BIMB Securities said the domestic banking sector and infrastructure-related stocks were expected to provide some insulation against external market volatility, supported by Malaysia's underlying economic resilience and infrastructure investment pipeline.
It added that robust domestic fundamentals could help cushion the impact of weaker global technology and commodity markets, although they were unlikely to drive aggressive gains in the benchmark index in the near term.
"Institutional capital is actively retreating from high-alpha tech and commodity proxies, exploiting robust domestic banking fundamentals to protect against ongoing capital flight from the US chip stock collapse and plunging crude oil and CPO prices," it said.
For its preferred stocks, the firm maintained a "Buy" call on Gamuda Bhd, Inari Amertron Bhd and Dialog Group Bhd, with target prices of RM5.91, RM2.90 and RM2.40 respectively.
It also identified CIMB Group Holdings and Malayan Banking as preferred banking exposures, although both were not rated.
The key risks to watch include tighter AI regulations in the US, potential supply chain disruptions and further weakness in crude oil and crude palm oil prices, which could weigh on corporate earnings and trigger further portfolio reallocation.

Title: Melaka polls: Former assemblyman rallies behind Tuminah in Pantai Kundor
Article:
MELAKA: Former Pantai Kundor assemblyman Datuk Nor Azman Hassan is putting past political differences aside to help Barisan Nasional candidate Datuk Tuminah Kadi defend the seat in the Melaka election.
Nor Azman, who won the seat for BN in the 2018 General Election, lost to Tuminah in the 2021 Melaka election when he contested as a Pakatan Harapan candidate.
Tuminah, who represented Umno, defeated Nor Azman by a majority of 827 votes.
Nor Azman's Umno membership was terminated in October 2021 after he joined three other assemblymen in withdrawing support for the Melaka state government led by then Chief Minister Datuk Seri Sulaiman Md Ali.
He rejoined Umno in July this year through the party's Rumah Bangsa initiative.
Speaking at a Pentas Gelombang Biru ceramah for the Pantai Kundor constituency in Tangga Batu here last night, Nor Azman said past disagreements with Tuminah should not stand in the way of their shared goal of retaining the seat for BN.
"Although we have had disagreements in the past, we are like a family in BN and our relationship will not be severed," he said.
Nor Azman, who is now the Pantai Kundor election director, said he was confident BN would retain the seat, which had never been lost by the coalition.
He cautioned Pantai Kundor voters against making a choice that could result in BN becoming the opposition in its own state. He said the coalition's campaign machinery needed to be more active in reaching out to various segments of society, including Pas leaders, non-governmental organisations (NGOs) and young voters.
"BN has never lost in Pantai Kundor, so I hope voters will not regret their decision later.
"I am confident BN will govern Melaka as promised," he said.
Nor Azman said he believed Tuminah could serve the people of Pantai Kundor well and help secure another seat for BN.
He said supporting the party's candidate was his responsibility, even though he was no longer contesting the seat.
.Also present at the ceramah were Umno secretary-general Datuk Dr Asyraf Wajdi Dusuki, Perikatan Nasional  secretary-general Datuk Seri Takiyuddin Hassan and Tuminah
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: S$4k offer lands Singaporean in RM1.5mil cannabis bust
Article:
IPOH: A 29-year-old Singaporean man was arrested with 19.04kg of cannabis worth RM1.52 million after accepting an offer of S$4,000 (RM12,690) to transport luggage to London.
Perak police chief Datuk Mohd Alwi Zainal Abidin said the suspect was detained at Sultan Azlan Shah Airport (LTSAS) here at 6.20am on Sunday.
He said auxiliary police personnel spotted the suspicious luggage during a routine inspection at the airport's check-in counter.
"The suspect was scheduled to fly from Ipoh to Singapore before continuing his journey to London, England.
"An inspection of his Caggioni-branded luggage uncovered 36 plastic packets containing dried leaves suspected to be cannabis," he said at a press conference at the Perak Police Contingent Headquarters today.
Alwi said the drugs weighed 19.04kg and were estimated to be worth RM1.52 million. The amount was sufficient to supply 47,900 drug users.
He said initial investigations found that the suspect had responded to an online job offer promising an attractive payment to transport luggage allegedly containing high-quality counterfeit luxury goods to London.
"The suspect claimed he was told that the luggage contained counterfeit goods and that he had not opened it.
"We believe the syndicate's modus operandi was to lure people with lucrative job offers before exploiting them as drug mules to transport drugs overseas on commercial flights," he said.
Alwi said the suspect had flown from Singapore to Kuala Lumpur before travelling to Kajang, where police believed he had collected the drugs from a supplier.
"He then travelled to Ipoh by Grab and checked into a hotel here. He arrived on Saturday and was arrested the following morning," he said.
He said the syndicate appeared to have targeted less busy airports, including Ipoh, to smuggle drugs overseas.
"There is only one daily flight from Ipoh to Singapore, and the suspect's journey was connected to an onward flight to London.
"Had he managed to check in the luggage, he could have continued his journey to London," he said.
Alwi said the suspect was unemployed and had been promised S$4,000 to transport the luggage.
He added that a preliminary urine screening found no traces of drugs in the suspect's system. Checks also revealed that he had no previous criminal record.
The man has been remanded for seven days from yesterday, he said, adding that this was the second drug-smuggling incident involving LTSAS recorded this year.
The case is being investigated under Section 39B of the Dangerous Drugs Act 1952. The offence carries the death penalty or life imprisonment and whipping of at least 12 strokes upon conviction.
Alwi said the seizure was the result of continuous intelligence-gathering by the Narcotics Criminal Investigation Department (NCID), coupled with cooperation from members of the public.
"Police will not compromise with any party involved in possessing or trafficking drugs, or protecting drug-related activities, as these are serious offences under the law.
"The NCID remains committed to combating drugs to protect present and future generations. Drugs are the country's number one enemy," he said

Title: GOF seizes 1.2 tonnes of suspected smuggled rice in Tumpat
Article:
KOTA BARU: The General Operations Force (GOF) seized 1,216kg of various brands of rice suspected to have been smuggled from Thailand during a raid in Kampung Kubang Panjang, Tumpat, yesterday.
The rice, valued at RM4,864, was seized during Op Taring Wawasan Kelantan around 4pm after members of Strike Force Company B, Battalion 7 of the Kuantan GOF, spotted a suspicious Nissan Vanette van while patrolling the Kota Baru-Pengkalan Kubor route.
Southeast Brigade Commander Datuk Ahmad Radzi Hussain said the van driver attempted to flee upon noticing the presence of the police, but the vehicle skidded in Kampung Kubang Panjang.
An inspection uncovered 49 sacks of rice comprising 750kg bearing the Mangga label, 250kg of Nangka, 120kg of Serindit, 72kg of Angsa Mas and 24kg of Pisang.
"A 35-year-old man who was driving the van was detained for investigation," he said in a statement.
Preliminary investigations found that the rice was believed to have been brought in from Thailand through the illegal Pohon Tar base in Kuala Jambu before being transported to Pasir Puteh.
Radzi said the case had been referred to the Kelantan Padi and Rice Regulatory Department for further action under Section 20 of the National Padi and Rice Regulatory Act.
Apart from the rice, the authorities also seized the Nissan Vanette, valued at RM18,000, bringing the total value of the seizure to RM22,864.

Title: [UPDATED] Sungai Pertak water surge: Four more victims found dead
Article:
KUALA KUBU BARU: Four more victims of the water surge at Sungai Pertak were found dead this morning, bringing the death toll to five out of the eight people swept away by strong currents.
Selangor Fire and Rescue Department assistant operations director Ashrul Riezal Asbar said three victims were found trapped near Jambatan Senget, close to the Sungai Luit campsite around 9.20am.
"Another victim was found near the same area at 10.20am, about 1.2km from the incident site.
"Search and rescue (SAR) personnel are working to retrieve all the victims," he said.
Earlier, a 36-year-old local man was
found dead
near Jambatan Pertak around 1.30am today. The victim was identified as V. Vijiyan.
Ashrul Riezal said the SAR operation resumed this morning, with the search area divided into four sectors.
"Sector A covers the area from Lata Jebus to Lubuk Pertak, while Sector B stretches from Lubuk Pertak to Jambatan Dam.
"Sector C covers the Jambatan Dam area, while Sector D covers the dam area," he said.
In yesterday's incident, eight people were reported swept away by strong currents following a water surge at several locations along Sungai Pertak.
The missing victims comprised a Yemeni, four Indian nationals, a Nepalese, a Sri Lankan and a local man.
Apart from those swept away, several groups of visitors were also reported stranded at Lata Jebus, Sungai Luit Camp and Gunung Rajah.
The SAR operation involves the Fire and Rescue Department and several other rescue agencies, with a combined strength of 91 personnel.
