Title: Trump signals progress towards ending Iran war after Qatar PM meeting
Article:
WASHINGTON: US President Donald Trump said on Monday there was "positive momentum" toward ending the war with Iran after meeting Qatar's prime minister at the White House.
"I had an excellent conversation with Sheikh Mohammed bin Abdulrahman bin Jassim Al Thani," Trump said on Truth Social, adding that "much was discussed with respect to the Islamic Republic of Iran."
The meeting with the Qatari prime minister – a key mediator in the Iran war – is Trump's first with a foreign leader since his party's massive losses in the midterm elections.
In the weeks leading up to the vote, there was widespread speculation that US strikes against Iran would resume soon after.
However, Trump has talked down resuming the conflict while leaving the door open to further strikes.
In his post on Monday, Trump reiterated that the US was "locked and loaded," but that he believed further strikes were "quite unlikely" given that key US allies in the Gulf "would prefer the status quo."
"We are seeing positive momentum toward an end to this Conflict, and will ensure that America's interests are at all times protected," Trump said.
Trump's comments echoed early statements to CNN over the weekend when he said it was "highly unlikely" fighting would resume.
- 'IMAGINARY TALKS' -
Iranian officials meanwhile expressed defiance at the continued pressure from Washington.
The Islamic republic's top security chief, Mohsen Rezai, wrote on X late Monday that the US "flails like a desperate gambler," telling Washington to "fold your hand. Stop manufacturing fake news about imaginary talks."
Earlier, Teheran's top negotiator Mahammad Bagher Ghalibaf claimed on X that Israel was pushing the US deeper into conflict, adding that "unless Washington drops the 'Israel First' mindset, America and its allies are headed straight for a dark age."
On the ground in Iran, strikes – which have not been publicly acknowledged by the US military – are continuing, according to Iranian authorities.
The island of Qeshm, located in the Strait of Hormuz, was targeted overnight from Sunday to Monday, the provincial deputy governor stated on state television.
Trump has acknowledged that the highly unpopular war with Iran was at least partially responsible for the Republicans' defeat, not least because it has contributed to rising prices in the US economy.--AFP
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Floods, storm and landslide leave 422 evacuees at relief centres in Perak, Selangor
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 10 — A total of 422 evacuees from 119 families remain at temporary relief centres (PPS) in Perak and Selangor as of this morning.
In Perak, the State Disaster Management Committee (JPBN) Secretariat said the number of flood evacuees had dropped to 410 people from 114 families, compared with 419 people from 124 families last night.
It said all evacuees were currently housed at three PPS in two districts.
“Larut, Matang and Selama was the latest district to be affected by flooding, with 39 people from eight families evacuated to the PPS at Surau Kampung Simpang Halt last night.
“In Hilir Perak, 238 flood evacuees from 69 families are housed at the Teluk Intan Municipal Council (MPTI) Rest House Hall, while another 133 from 37 families are taking shelter at the MPTI Langkap Hall,” the secretariat said in a statement.
Meanwhile, in Selangor, 12 storm victims from three families remain at the PPS at Dewan Sri Bernam in Sabak Bernam, according to the Social Welfare Department's (JKM) InfoBencana portal.
Another 20 people from five families displaced by a landslide in Gombak on October 29 remain at the PPS at Balai Raya Kampung Kenanga. — Bernama

Title: DAP committed to nation-building regardless of govt or opposition role, says veep Teo Nie Ching
Article:
KULAI, Nov 10 — The DAP wants to continue playing its role as a nation-building party, regardless of whether it is in government or the opposition, by championing transparent, fair and sustainable policies, said its vice-president Teo Nie Ching.
Teo, who is also deputy communications minister, said the principle formed the basis of DAP’s struggle to ensure Malaysia continued to develop as a nation with a sustainable governance system, while prioritising the interests and welfare of the people.
“Regardless of whether we are in the opposition or in government, we want to be a nation builder.
“… we want to develop our country together, and that is why we want to ensure that we can make Malaysia a country with a sustainable system,” she said in an exclusive interview with Bernama recently.
The Wanita DAP chief said the party’s contribution to nation-building was not confined to economic and physical development, but also included efforts to strengthen inclusive and fair policies, including taking into account the needs of women and children.
Commenting on DAP’s participation in the Madani Government, Teo said its position provided the party with an opportunity to translate its principles into policies and action through direct involvement in the country’s administration.
The Kulai MP said the priority was to ensure that the policies it championed could be implemented transparently and benefit the people, thereby contributing to the country’s long-term development.
“Our intention is to ensure that we can contribute to nation-building by ensuring that we have policies that are more open and transparent,” she said.
Asked about DAP’s approach ahead of the 16th General Election, Teo said the party left it to the people to make their own assessment, but efforts to win over voters should be based on its achievements and track record during its time in government.
She cited the establishment of the Malaysian Media Council (MMM), which was among the reform agendas championed by the party for more than 50 years before being realised through the passage of the Malaysian Media Council Act under the Madani Government.
“Malaysia now has the MMM, chaired by a former Federal Court judge, demonstrating the efforts to realise the institutional reform agenda under the Madani Government.
“In addition, Pakatan Harapan has also championed the proposal to limit the Prime Minister’s term of office, with Penang becoming the first state to amend its state constitution to limit the Chief Minister’s tenure to 10 years. The agenda was subsequently brought to the federal government level, with the hope that the proposal would be passed in the Dewan Rakyat,” she said.
Touching on the challenges of implementing policies while in government, Teo said not all decisions received the support of every party, particularly when the interests of certain groups were involved.
She said this was among the challenges faced by parties in government, but their track record in implementing policies should serve as evidence to the people of the efforts undertaken.
“I believe that being in government does come with its pros and cons. The cons are quite obvious because not all policies will be supported by everyone.
“...when we, for example, decided to raise the minimum wage to RM2,000, there are business people and employers who disagree with that direction. But I think what is most important is that we show voters our track record so that they will be willing to give DAP a chance,” she said. — Bernama

Title: Too early for a Cabinet reshuffle, says Anwar
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 10 — Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim today said it was too early to discuss a Cabinet reshuffle amid speculation over possible changes to the line-up following Transport Minister Anthony Loke’s decision to resign.
When reporters asked when the reshuffle would take place after he officiated the International Construction Week and BuildXPO Malaysia 2026 at the Malaysia International Trade and Exhibition Centre (Mitec) here, Anwar briefly replied: “It’s too early.”
Loke had previously indicated that tomorrow’s ministry event may or may not be his final engagement with Transport Ministry staff, although he did not confirm whether it would serve as his farewell.
Loke announced his intention to resign on November 6, following DAP’s objection to the conditional pardon allowing former prime minister Datuk Seri Najib Razak to serve the remainder of his prison sentence under house arrest.
He said his resignation would take effect once Najib arrived at his residence and that he would submit an additional letter to Anwar to formalise his departure.
Utusan Malaysia
reported today that the Cabinet could see changes involving two positions, namely the Transport Minister’s post following Loke’s resignation and the Second Finance Minister’s position held by Datuk Seri Amir Hamzah Azizan, whose three-year term as a senator is due to expire on December 11.
Amir Hamzah could retain his portfolio, but he would need to be reappointed to the Senate and sworn in again before resuming his Cabinet duties
The report, citing sources, said any reshuffle was likely to be limited to the two positions rather than a major Cabinet overhaul.
The last Cabinet reshuffle took place on December 16 last year.

Title: Melaka polls: EC targets 95pc early voter turnout as 53.25pc cast ballots by 10.35am
Article:
MELAKA, Nov 10 — The Election Commission (EC) is targeting a voter turnout of up to 95 per cent for the early voting phase of the 16th Melaka state election today.
EC chairman Datuk Seri Ramlan Harun said as of 10.35 am, 53.25 per cent or 5,286 early voters had cast their ballots across 31 polling centres, which comprise 50 polling streams.
He noted that 19 early voting streams with a lower number of voters will close at noon today, while the remaining streams will close in stages at 2 pm and 5 pm.
“Today, 9,769 military personnel and 2,762 police personnel are participating in the early voting process, bringing the total number of early voters to 12,531,” he said.
Ramlan made these remarks while speaking to reporters after observing the early voting process for the 16th Melaka state election at Sekolah Menengah Kebangsaan Kem Terendak in Sungai Udang, here, today.
In a related development, Ramlan mentioned that the EC has received 237 reports concerning election offences throughout the campaign period, which began following the nomination of candidates on October 31.
“The violations, among other things, relate to minor infractions under election regulations that occurred during campaigning involving issues such as the display of contesting parties’ flags and campaign materials.
“Otherwise, everything has proceeded well and smoothly, with no major incidents reported. I hope this trend continues throughout the remainder of the campaign period, and I urge everyone to remain prudent and orderly, and to avoid causing any disruptions,” he said.
A total of 79 candidates representing various political parties and coalitions, as well as independent candidates are eligible to contest in this Melaka state election.
The Election Commission (EC) has set November 14 as the polling day for the Melaka state election, while early voting is taking place today.
For the latest updates on the 16th Melaka state election, please visit https://election.bernama.com/prn/melaka/2026. — Bernama

Title: Malaysia aims to build one million affordable homes by 2035 using advanced construction technology, says Anwar
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 10 — Malaysia aims to deliver 500,000 affordable homes by 2030 and one million by 2035 through the adoption and development of advanced modular construction technology, Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim said today.
He said technology must help the country build homes more efficiently and affordably without compromising safety, quality and liveability.
“For example, the 13th Malaysia Plan. We set up a target of delivering 500,000 affordable homes by 2030. It’s part of our wider national aspiration for 1 million homes between 2036 and  2035.
“Now technology must help us deliver these homes more efficiently, without compromising forsafety, quality and liveability,” he said when officiating the International Construction Week and BuildXPO Malaysia 2026 at the Malaysia International Trade and Exhibition Centre (Mitec) here.
MORE TO COME

Title: EC, MCMC take measures to protect website following reported cyber attack
Article:
MELAKA, Nov 10 — The Election Commission (EC) is working with the Malaysian Communications and Multimedia Commission (MCMC) and other relevant parties to strengthen the security of its website following reports of a suspected cyber attack.
EC chairman Datuk Seri Ramlan Harun said a report on the incident had also been submitted to the relevant authorities as an initial measure to ensure the commission’s systems remain protected.
“We have already worked with all relevant authorities to ensure that this does not happen again. Insya Allah,” God willing,” he told reporters.
He was met after inspecting the early voting process for the 16th Melaka State Election at Sekolah Menengah Kem Terendak in Sungai Udang today.
Ramlan said the EC would also issue an official statement on the matter soon.
“I have yet to receive a full report on the matter, but Insya Allah, the EC will issue an official statement soon.
“Let us all hope that the cyber attack does not affect our website, as it is very important to the smooth implementation of the election,” he said.
Earlier, an EC live broadcast on social media announced that the commission’s website was believed to be facing a cyber attack threat.
For the latest updates on the 16th Melaka State Election, visit https://election.bernama.com/pm/melaka/2026/. — Bernama

Title: Melaka polls: Police receive 19 reports, open 18 investigation papers, make no arrests
Article:
MELAKA, Nov 10 — Melaka police have received 19 reports involving various offences, including mischief, mischief by fire and fighting, since campaigning for the 16th Melaka state election began on October 31.
Its chief Datuk Dzulkhairi Mukhtar said 18 investigation papers had been opened over the 11-day period, but no arrests had been made so far.
“Most of the cases are being investigated under Section 427 of the Penal Code for mischief and Section 435 for mischief by fire, particularly incidents involving the burning of flags.
“There have also been cases of incitement and intimidation,” he told reporters after casting his ballot in early voting at the multipurpose hall of the Melaka Police Contingent headquarters in Bukit Beruang here today.
He said campaigning had been peaceful and orderly so far, with no untoward incidents reported.
Dzulkhairi said 669 police personnel had been deployed across the state to monitor election campaigning and maintain public safety and order.
On preparations for polling day this Saturday, he said 3,332 police personnel would be deployed, including officers assigned to monitor the voting process at polling centres throughout the state.
He said the Cantas team would also be deployed on polling day, warning that police would not hesitate to make arrests if any disturbances occurred.
He also urged political party supporters to behave responsibly, abide by the law and refrain from intimidating or coercing voters.
For the latest news on the 16th Melaka state election, visit https://election.bernama.com/prn/melaka/2026/. — Bernama

Title: Singaporean lured by RM12,685 job offer arrested, remanded seven days over RM1.5m cannabis haul at Ipoh Airport
Article:
IPOH, Nov 10 — A S$4,000 (RM12,685) job to deliver a package landed a 29-year-old Singaporean in trouble after police found RM1.5 million worth of dried cannabis leaves in his luggage at the Sultan Azlan Shah Airport here on Sunday.
Perak police chief Commissioner Datuk Mohd Alwi Zainal Abidin said the suspect had been tricked by a syndicate into believing he was transporting a package containing counterfeit luxury-branded goods.
“Preliminary investigations found that the suspect had come across a job offer through a website promising lucrative payment to transport luggage allegedly containing counterfeit luxury-branded goods to London, England,” he told a press conference at the Perak Police Headquarters here.
He said that the syndicate was believed to have targeted less busy airports, concealing drugs in passengers’ luggage to avoid detection by the authorities.
“If the luggage passes through Customs at these airports, the items will then be sent as cargo and eventually reach their intended destination,” he said.
Mohd Alwi said the suspect was arrested after auxiliary police personnel at the airport detected a suspicious piece of luggage during a baggage inspection at the check-in counter at about 6.20am on November 8.
He said the suspect was scheduled to fly from Ipoh to Singapore, where he would transit before continuing to London.
“Further inspection of the Caggioni-branded zippered suitcase found 36 transparent plastic packets containing dried leaves suspected to be cannabis flower.
“The drugs weighed approximately 19,040 grammes and had an estimated street value of RM1,523,200,” he said.
Mohd Alwi said the amount of drugs seized could have been used by about 47,900 addicts.
He said the suspect and the seized items were subsequently handed over to the Perak Narcotics Criminal Investigation Department (NCID) for further investigation.
“A preliminary urine screening found that the suspect tested negative for drugs, while checks also found that he had no previous criminal record,” he said.
He also added that the suspect, who is currently unemployed, had been remanded for seven days since November 8.
Mohd Alwi said the case was being investigated under Section 39B of the Dangerous Drugs Act 1952.
“If convicted, the offence carries the death penalty or life imprisonment and whipping of not less than 12 strokes,” he said.
He said the seizure was the result of continuous intelligence-gathering efforts by the NCID, with cooperation from members of the public.
“We will not compromise with any party involved in drug trafficking.
“Possessing, distributing or protecting drug-related activities is a serious offence under the law,” he said.

Title: Water surge at Pertak river: Four more bodies found, bringing toll to five
Article:
HULU SELANGOR, Nov 10 — Four more bodies of victims swept away by strong currents at Sungai Pertak in Kuala Kubu Bharu were found this morning, bringing the number of victims located to five out of the eight reported missing.
Selangor Fire and Rescue Department assistant operations director Ashrul Riezal Asbar said three victims were found trapped near Jambatan Senget, close to the Sungai Luit campsite, at 9.20am,
Utusan Malaysia
reported.
“Another victim was found near the same area at 10.20am, about 1.2km from the incident site.
“Rescue teams are now working to retrieve all the victims,” he said.
The incident occurred at about 5.55pm yesterday, when eight people — comprising one Yemeni national, one Malaysian, one Sri Lankan, one Nepalese and four Indian nationals — were swept away by the current.
A 36-year-old local man was found dead near Jambatan Pertak at about 1.30am today.
The search and rescue operation resumed this morning, with the search area divided into four sectors around the incident site as teams continued efforts to locate the three remaining missing victims.

Title: Najib house arrest: Home minister says court must clarify Prisons Dept’s authority
Article:
MELAKA, Nov 10 — The interpretation of the Conditional Pardon Order and the implications of the Order of Discharge involving Datuk Seri Najib Tun Razak require further clarification to establish whether the Prisons Department has the authority to implement house arrest for the former prime minister.
Home Affairs Minister Datuk Seri Saifuddin Nasution Ismail said the department, as the implementing agency, needed to ensure that its actions did not result in wrongful detention.
“We are the implementing agency. The Order of Discharge states that he is to be released, whereas the Pardons Board refers to house arrest. House arrest is different from release. So, from our position, which one should we follow? These are legal documents and if there is any ambiguity, we refer the matter to the court.
“The wording used is ‘discharge forthwith’, meaning release. In prison terminology, there are distinctions between release, discharge and discharge not amounting to acquittal. If discharge means that he is released, then the Prisons Department no longer has any authority over him. But if it is house arrest, the department still has authority,” he told reporters.
Saifuddin was commenting on a statement by the Attorney General’s Chambers (AGC) last Friday that the implementation of house arrest for Najib had been temporarily deferred pending further examination of the Conditional Pardon Order and the implications of the Order of Discharge issued by the High Court in Kuala Lumpur, following the settlement of the RM50 million fine.
Elaborating, he said the Order of Discharge was issued by the Registrar of the High Court, prompting the ministry to seek the AGC’s views on the matter.
“Who issued this Order of Discharge? It was issued by the Registrar of the High Court. That is why we sought the AGC’s views and, as explained, the matter will be brought before the court to clarify the two differing interpretations,” he said.
He said he had no information on which party would bring the matter before the court or when a decision would be made.
“However, I wish to stress that this is purely a matter of interpretation. We comply with, respect and accept the notification of the house arrest order for Najib, as stated in the letter sent by the Secretary of the Pardons Board to the Home Ministry,” he said.
Saifuddin was speaking after attending an engagement and dialogue session with fishermen at the Lereh Tanjung Kling Fishermen’s Jetty here yesterday, which was also attended by Malaysian Fisheries Development Authority (LKIM) chairman Muhammad Faiz Fadzil.
In an earlier statement, the AGC said Najib would remain at his current place of detention throughout the period of deferment, subject to the authority and directions of the relevant authorities.
Najib paid the RM50 million fine imposed on him in the SRC International funds misappropriation case at the High Court Criminal Registry Office last Friday. — Bernama

Title: GOF seizes 1.2 tonnes of suspected Thai smuggled rice in Tumpat
Article:
KOTA BHARU, Nov 10 — The General Operations Force (GOF) seized 1,216 kilogrammes of various brands of rice suspected to have been smuggled from Thailand during a raid in Kampung Kubang Panjang, Tumpat, yesterday.
The seizure, valued at RM4,864, was made during Op Taring Wawasan Kelantan at about 4pm after members of Strike Force Company B, Battalion 7 of the Kuantan GOF, spotted a suspicious Nissan Vanette van while patrolling the Kota Bharu-Pengkalan Kubor route.
South-east Brigade Commander Datuk Ahmad Radzi Hussain said the van driver allegedly attempted to flee upon noticing the presence of the police, but the vehicle subsequently skidded in the Kampung Kubang Panjang area.
An inspection of the van uncovered 49 sacks of rice of various brands, comprising 750 kg bearing the Mangga label, 250 kg with the Nangka label, 120 kg with the Serindit label, 72 kg with the Angsa Mas label and 24 kg with the Pisang label.
“A 35-year-old local man who was driving the van was detained for investigation,” he said in a statement.
Preliminary investigations revealed that the rice was believed to have been brought in from Thailand through the illegal Pohon Tar base in Kuala Jambu before being transported to Pasir Puteh.
Ahmad Radzi said the case had been handed over to the Kelantan State Padi and Rice Regulatory Department for further action under Section 20 of the National Padi and Rice Regulatory Act 1994.
Apart from the rice, the authorities also seized the Nissan Vanette van, valued at RM18,000, bringing the total value of the seizure to RM22,864. — Bernama

Title: Melaka polls: Pakatan’s Jegasilan wants to create jobs in Gadek through modern farming
Article:
ALOR GAJAH, Nov 10 — Gadek has the potential to become a hub for modern agriculture and livestock farming, creating job opportunities for local youths and reducing their need to seek employment elsewhere, particularly in Singapore.
Pakatan Harapan (PH) candidate for the Gadek state seat, Jegasilan K, 45, said the area still had vast tracts of land that could be developed for modern vegetable cultivation and livestock farming.
He said former rubber plantations could be transformed into agricultural areas producing various crops for local markets, alongside livestock hubs for poultry and cattle.
“As a local, I see considerable potential to expand modern agriculture in the villages around Gadek, particularly through livestock farming and vegetable cultivation.
“We can introduce various crops that can penetrate local markets while developing poultry and cattle farming hubs here,” he told Bernama.
Jegasilan, who runs a tuition centre, said local youths could spearhead these initiatives if given appropriate training and guidance.
He said developing local employment opportunities could help reduce the number of young people migrating to Singapore, where working away from home often made it difficult for them to return during emergencies and festive occasions.
Apart from agriculture, he said Gadek also had potential to become a tourism destination, citing its waterfalls, hot springs, accommodation facilities and other natural attractions.
He said these attractions could be further developed by tapping the ideas and abilities of local youths.
On his campaign, Jegasilan said he had received encouraging responses from Malay, Chinese and Indian residents during his house-to-house visits over the past week.
He said water supply, drainage and road conditions were among the issues frequently raised, while residents also wanted an elected representative who remained approachable and accessible after taking office.
“They do not want a ‘weekly representative’, but someone who remains close to the people and is easy to reach whenever problems arise,” he said.
Jegasilan faces three challengers in the Gadek state seat contest — S. Nadarajah of Barisan Nasional (BN), Laveen Balaprabhakaran (Bersama) and Laila Norinda Maon (Putra).
Polling is set for November 14, with early voting on November 10.
For the latest news on the 16th Melaka state election, visit https://election.bernama.com/prn/melaka/2026/. — Bernama

Title: MOE gets 670 school maintenance applications in first week of special channel, says Fadhlina
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 10 — The Ministry of Education (MOE) has received 670 applications from Parent-Teacher Associations (PTAs) nationwide for school maintenance allocations, just a week after the launch of the MOE PTA special channel on November 1.
Education Minister Datuk Seri Fadhlina Sidek, in a Facebook post today, said the strong response reflected PTAs’ commitment to working together with the ministry to improve school facilities and create a more conducive environment for students.
“I am happy to see this response. It shows the determination of PTAs to work together to help improve school facilities and environments for the comfort of our children,” she said.
She said the ministry hoped to see PTAs play a greater role as strategic partners in efforts to strengthen the country’s education ecosystem.
According to Fadhlina, parents who send their children to school daily also have valuable insights into areas that require attention and improvement.
Meanwhile, she said applications for school maintenance allocations through the special channel remain open until November 30, giving PTAs that have yet to apply an opportunity to submit their requests.
Previously, the media reported that Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim had announced an allocation of RM2 billion to the MOE under Budget 2027 for the repair and maintenance of all types of schools nationwide. — Bernama

Title: Penang water operator boosts security after vandalism, theft at Pokok Sena canal
Article:
BUTTERWORTH, Nov 10 — The Penang Water Supply Corporation (PBAPP) has tightened security and stepped up patrols along the Pokok Sena Canal here following incidents of trespassing, vandalism and theft.
In a statement today, PBAPP said the incidents came to light during a routine security patrol by its auxiliary police, with subsequent checks revealing that several infrastructure components in the canal area had been damaged or were missing.
PBAPP subsequently lodged a police report at 1.07pm yesterday to facilitate further investigations into the incidents.
“Following the incident, PBAPP has tightened security and stepped up patrols in the area to safeguard its assets and ensure the smooth release of water from the Mengkuang Dam through the Pokok Sena Canal,” it said in the statement posted on Facebook.
PBAPP also urged anyone with information on the incidents or who witnesses suspicious activity in the area to report it to the authorities. — Bernama

Title: North-east monsoon: Kelantan Fire Dept readies 35 boats for flood rescues
Article:
KOTA BHARU, Nov 10 — A total of 35 of the 45 boats belonging to the Kelantan Fire and Rescue Department (JBPM) are operational and ready for deployment during the 2026/2027 North-east Monsoon, said its director Farhan Sufyan Borhan.
He said inspections and tests had been conducted to assess the operational readiness of the department’s water rescue equipment and identify boats that could be repaired and returned to service.
“We have a total of 45 boats, of which 35 are operational while the remaining 10 are in poor condition,” he told Bernama recently.
Farhan Sufyan said boats were among the most critical assets in flood rescue operations, particularly in flooded areas inaccessible to land vehicles.
However, he said the department’s operational requirements extended beyond boats, with land vehicles also playing a vital role in evacuating flood victims and delivering food and other essential supplies to affected areas.
Farhan Sufyan said the department would ensure that all available assets remained on standby to respond to possible flooding throughout the monsoon season.
He said additional lorries and four-wheel-drive vehicles were needed to strengthen the department’s logistical capacity, particularly in supporting flood rescue operations and the distribution of relief supplies.
The department currently has eight three- and five-tonne lorries and 30 four-wheel-drive vehicles stationed at 22 fire stations across Kelantan, he said.
“Our most pressing need is for additional lorries and four-wheel-drive vehicles. There are already many boats available, not just within the JBPM but also in other agencies,” he said.
He said land transport was essential for delivering relief supplies, particularly during large-scale rescue operations that required sustained logistical support across extensive areas.
Farhan Sufyan said additional transport assets would help enhance the department’s operational efficiency in the event of major flooding in Kelantan.
Last Sunday, the Malaysian Meteorological Department (MetMalaysia) issued an alert-level continuous rain warning for several areas in Kelantan, Pahang and Sabah, as well as the whole of Terengganu, valid until Wednesday.
MetMalaysia said the warning covered Tanah Merah, Pasir Mas, Tumpat, Kota Bharu, Machang, Bachok, Pasir Puteh, Kuala Krai and Jeli in Kelantan.
Following the continuous rain warning, the National Flood Forecasting and Warning Centre of the Department of Irrigation and Drainage warned of possible flooding in nine districts in Kelantan from today until Wednesday. — Bernama

Title: Melaka polls: Early voting begins smoothly as security personnel turn out
Article:
MELAKA, Nov 10 — The early voting process for the 16th Melaka state election proceeded smoothly this morning, with many security personnel taking advantage of the clear weather early in the day to arrive at the polling centres.
At the polling centre located in the multipurpose hall of the Melaka police contingent headquarters (IPK), a Bernama observation noted that eligible police personnel began arriving as early as 7.30am, lining up to cast their votes starting at 7.53am.
The voting process remained orderly after the polls opened at 8am at the centre situated within the Ayer Keroh state constituency with the assistance of Election Commission (EC) officials.
A total of 817 police personnel are set to cast their early votes at this location.
Melaka police chief Datuk Dzulkhairi Mukhtar, who arrived at 7.52am, took the time to observe the voting process before casting his own vote at polling stream 1 (saluran satu) at 8.42am.
The Ayer Keroh state constituency is seeing a four-way contest involving incumbent, Kerk Chee Yee (Pakatan Harapan), as well as Datuk Seri Michael Gan Peng Lam (Perikatan Nasional), Muhammad Muhaimin Lau Abdullah (Parti Bersama Malaysia), and Mohd Hamnaim Mohamad (Parti Pribumi Bersatu Malaysia).
Mohd Hamnaim was also seen observing the voting process at the centre.
At Kem Terendak in Sungai Udang, the voting process proceeded in an orderly manner as military personnel and their spouses arrived to cast their ballots, with polling stations at the camp opening at 8am.
Some voters arrived accompanied by their children, drawing the attention of media personnel who captured the antics of the little ones as they tagged along with their parents to the polling stations early in the morning.
Voters first verified their names and personal details at counters set up by the military before proceeding to their respective polling streams, while Election Commission (EC) officials were on hand to assist voters with information regarding the voting process.
Three polling centres were opened at the camp: Sekolah Kebangsaan (SK) Kem Terendak I, with six streams and 2,850 voters; SK Kem Terendak II, with six streams and 2,660 voters; and Sekolah Menengah Kebangsaan Kem Terendak, which featured five streams and 2,189 voters.
In total, 31 early voting centres for the 16th Melaka state election opened promptly at 8am today, allowing 12,531 security personnel and their spouses to exercise their democratic rights.
According to EC statistics, 9,769 military personnel and their spouses, along with 2,762 police personnel, are set to cast their votes.
The polling centres will close in stages at 12pm, 2pm, and 5pm today in accordance with the schedule established by the EC.
In total, 687,697 voters are eligible to cast their ballots in this Melaka state election and EC has designated today for early voting, while November 14 has been set as the main polling day.
For the latest news on the 16th Melaka state election, visit https://election.bernama.com/pm/melaka/2026/. — Bernama

Title: Two burnt to death, two injured as Mercedes catches fire after crash in Johor Bahru
Article:
JOHOR BAHRU, Nov 10 — Two people were burnt to death while two others were injured after a car they were travelling in caught fire, following an accident near the Permas Jaya Golf Club, along the road heading towards Bakar Batu, early today.
Johor Jaya Fire and Rescue Station (BBP) Operations Commander PBK I Razali Hussein said the department received an emergency call about the incident at about 4.35am.
He said firefighters who arrived at the scene found the car, a Mercedes, believed to have skidded and overturned by the roadside, about 90 per cent burnt.
“Five people were in the car. Two of them were found burnt inside the vehicle, while three others managed to escape from the vehicle before firefighters arrived,” he said in a statement today.
He said of the three who escaped from the burning vehicle, two of them were injured and sent to Sultan Ismail Hospital (HSI) for treatment, while the other was not injured.
The bodies of the two victims were subsequently handed over to the police for further action. — Bernama

Title: Melaka polls: Pakatan’s Ginie Lim uses interactive digital platform to reach Machap Jaya voters
Article:
MELAKA, Nov 10 — The Pakatan Harapan (PH) candidate for Machap Jaya state constituency, Datuk Ginie Lim Siew Lin, is leveraging on an interactive digital platform to reach out to voters for the Melaka state election and to enhance their understanding of the electoral process.
Through the website https://ginielim.com/, voters can access a wealth of information about the candidate including her biography, background, manifesto, and campaign tour schedule while also engaging through various provided communication channels.
Lim noted that the platform features an interactive game that challenges users to reach 8,015 clicks within 90 seconds, encouraging participation, alongside a simulation game designed to demonstrate the correct voting procedure.
She explained that the simulation game was specifically created to help first-time voters understand how to mark a ballot paper emphasising the importance of making a single, correct mark in the space designated for their chosen candidate to ensure the vote remains valid.
“Additionally, there is a scenario-based game that allows voters to select proposed solutions for specific issues, such as the challenges faced by wheelchair users when leaving their homes.”
“The platform also showcases my manifesto, which is anchored in four key pillars: Accessible Service, Safe Community, Prosperous Living, and a Thriving Economy,” she told Bernama here recently.
Lim added that voters can also obtain information regarding campaign tour activities and contact her team via a WhatsApp link integrated into the website.
According to her, the platform is accessible through a web browser without the need for users to download any applications, making it convenient for the public to access the provided information.
“This initiative was developed with careful consideration for concerns regarding the potential misuse of artificial intelligence (AI) technology. In the context of an election, I would be quite saddened if any party were to use AI to disparage their opponents; therefore, my team and I have devised creative and innovative ways to engage with voters.
“AI can be utilised for various purposes and functions. Consequently, we have explored more interactive methods to disseminate information and assist voters in making informed choices based on the data they receive,” she said.
The Machap Jaya state constituency will see a three-way contest between Lim, incumbent Datuk Ngwe Hee Sem of Barisan Nasional, and Prasanth Kumar Brakasam of Parti Bersama Malaysia.
The Election Commission has scheduled early voting for the 16th Melaka state election for today, with the main polling day set for November 14.
For the latest updates on the 16th Melaka state election, please visit https://election.bernama.com/prn/melaka/2026/. — Bernama

Title: Factory worker killed after motorcycle crashes into Proton that veered into his path in Kluang
Article:
KLUANG, Nov 10 — A factory worker was killed yesterday after his Yamaha motorcycle crashed into a car that had veered into his path along Jalan Anggerik near Felda Kahang Barat.
The 4.30pm collision killed Muhammad Azrin Zahiruddin, 22, at the scene due to severe injuries to his body and head, Kosmo! Online reported.
Kluang district police chief Assistant Commissioner Bahrin Mohd Noh said the victim was travelling from Gunung Berlumut towards Jalan Padang Tembak when the accident occurred.
At the same time, a Proton car driven by a 29-year-old man was travelling in the opposite direction, while a Toyota driven by a 45-year-old man with two passengers was behind the victim.
“Initial investigations found that the Proton driver lost control of his vehicle, causing it to enter the opposite lane before colliding with the victim’s motorcycle.
“The Toyota, which was unable to avoid the collision, crashed into the rear of the Proton,” he said in a statement today.
The victim’s body was sent to Enche’ Besar Hajjah Khalsom Hospital in Kluang for a post-mortem.

Title: Gardenia East Malaysia issues corporate clarification amid food poisoning case
Article:
KOTA KINABALU, Nov 10 — Gardenia Bakeries (East Malaysia) Sdn Bhd has clarified that it is a separate business entity from Gardenia Bakeries (KL) Sdn Bhd, following complaints of alleged food poisoning involving Gardenia products that have attracted public attention on social media.
Kim Teck Cheong Consolidated Berhad Executive Director Datuk Dexter Lau, said the two companies have different ownership and management structures.
“Gardenia Bakeries (East Malaysia) Sdn Bhd and Gardenia Bakeries (KL) Sdn Bhd are two separate business entities with different ownership and management structures,” he said in a statement on Sunday.
Lau’s clarification comes amid a Ministry of Health (MoH) investigation into complaints of alleged food poisoning after consuming Gardenia Original Classic White Bread and Twiggies Choc-A-Lot.
On November 8, the ministry said preliminary investigations were underway and that it was awaiting laboratory analysis results from samples collected from complainants.
The ministry said it had sought an explanation from Gardenia Bakeries (KL), whose internal investigation reportedly found no irregularities in production processes, recipe changes or compliance with standard operating procedures and food safety controls.
However, MoH clarified that the company’s findings could not be taken as a definitive conclusion on the cause of the symptoms reported.
It said product traceability remained limited due to incomplete batch numbers and expiry dates provided by complainants.
The ministry said it would conduct follow-up inspections at the Kuala Lumpur factory to verify compliance with the Food Act 1983 and take appropriate enforcement action if any violations or food safety risks were established.
Meanwhile, Lau assured consumers that food safety, hygiene, quality control and compliance with established standards and regulations remained top priorities in every aspect of Gardenia Bakeries (East Malaysia)’s operations.
He stressed that the company remained committed to ensuring that every product it manufactured met the prescribed food safety and quality standards.
“We appreciate the continued trust and support of our consumers and will continue striving to uphold our commitment to providing safe and high-quality products,” he added. — The Borneo Post

Title: Sarawak to keep pushing for greater rights under MA63, says Abang Johari
Article:
SEBAUH, Nov 10 — Sarawak will continue defending its rights under the Malaysia Agreement 1963 (MA63), said caretaker Premier Tan Sri Abang Johari Openg.
“As long as I am leading, I will not back down on our rights under MA63,” he said, adding the matter was a responsibility to the people.
He said this in his speech when officiating for the Batang Kemena Bridge opening ceremony in Sebauh here yesterday.
Abang Johari said the state’s position was strengthened by unity among its people and the state’s political leadership.
“We fought based on facts and our rights under MA63. With us united, there are many people behind me,” he said.
He said Sarawak’s decision to pursue greater control over its resources, particularly in the oil and gas sector, was part of efforts to strengthen the state’s economic position.
“I established Petros because it is a Sarawak entity that can participate in the oil and gas industry,” he said.
He said Sarawak’s economic strategy was aimed at increasing state revenue so that more funds could be channelled into infrastructure, education, healthcare and other areas benefiting the people.
Abang Johari also stressed that Sarawak’s development approach was not intended to exclude other parts of Malaysia, saying the state would continue to contribute to the country while safeguarding its own interests.
Also present were caretaker Deputy Premier Datuk Amar Douglas Uggah Embas; Sarawak Legislative Assembly Speaker Tan Sri Datuk Amar Mohamad Asfia Awang Nassar; Malaysia Tourism, Arts and Culture Minister Datuk Seri Tiong King Sing; caretaker Minister for Food Industry, Commodity and Regional Development Dato Sri Dr Stephen Rundi Utom; Sarawak State Secretary Datuk Amar Mohamad Abu Bakar Marzuki; and Bintulu Resident Datu Nyurak Keti. — The Borneo Post

Title: Cyber threats to Malaysia now extend beyond data theft to daily disruption, Nacsa says
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 10 — Cybercriminals are increasingly shifting their focus beyond mere data theft to disrupting people’s daily lives through attacks on physical systems and operational technology (OT).
National Cyber Security Agency (Nacsa) Chief Executive Dr Megat Zuhairy Megat Tajuddin said Malaysia was not exempt from this threat, particularly attacks targeting industrial control systems in the healthcare, energy, water supply and supply chain sectors.
Citing recent incidents in Europe, he said breaches that crippled supermarket operations and blood bank refrigeration systems demonstrated how a new generation of cyberattacks was deliberately designed to disrupt essential public services.
He said the situation had become more challenging with advances in artificial intelligence (AI), which enabled cybercriminals to launch automated and simultaneous intrusions against multiple organisations.
“This capability has increased the scale, speed and intensity of cyberattacks worldwide, and Malaysia, like other countries, is not exempt from the risk of facing similar modus operandi,” he told Bernama.
He explained that OT systems in these strategic sectors were highly vulnerable to attacks if connected directly to the internet without adequate protection.
In this regard, he said Nacsa urged National Critical Information Infrastructure (NCII) entities to isolate critical operational systems from external networks, while ensuring that their service continuity plans were regularly updated.
“No system is completely immune to attacks, but preparedness and the ability to recover quickly can reduce the impact of an incident on the public,” he said.
From a legal perspective, Megat Zuhairy stressed that the Cyber Security Act 2024 (Act 854) required NCII entities to comply with stringent security practices to ensure the resilience of their respective service systems.
For organisations that are not classified as NCII entities, Nacsa has issued the Cyber Security Threat Preparedness and Handling Guidelines as a reference to enhance preparedness, early detection, threat response and service continuity.
Commenting on the National Security Council’s (MKN) decision to raise the National Cyber Threat Level (NCTL) from Low to Moderate on Nov 4, he explained that the move was a proactive precautionary measure and did not mean the country was experiencing a cyber security crisis.
The move was followed by instructions to all sector leads and NCII entities to strengthen monitoring and submit regular weekly reports to Nacsa, even in the absence of any incidents.
“The increase in the NCTL to Moderate is a precautionary measure to enhance preparedness in advance, and not an indication that the country is facing a cyber security crisis.
“Cyber security is a shared responsibility, and everyone can contribute by adopting proper security practices and refraining from spreading unverified information,” he said.
To strengthen future defences, he said priority should be given to rapid threat intelligence sharing between the government and industry, local talent development and technology-assisted monitoring, including the use of AI.
He said regular training and incident simulation exercises were also important, while the establishment of the Cyber Security and Cryptology Development Centre (CSCDC) under Nacsa would further strengthen the country’s expertise and technological capabilities in cyber security. — Bernama

Title: Flood warning issued for low-lying areas in Jerantut, Rompin in Pahang from tomorrow
Article:
KUANTAN, Nov 10 — The National Flood Forecasting and Warning Centre (PRABN) of the Department of Irrigation and Drainage (DID) has issued a flood warning for Jerantut and Rompin, covering low-lying and high-risk areas within the respective river basins, from 1 am tomorrow (November 11) until 11.59pm on Saturday (November 14).
PRABN said in a statement that the flood forecast was based on a continuous rain warning (Alert level) issued by the Malaysian Meteorological Department at 8.30am yesterday, as well as projections from the DID’s flood forecasting model.
In Jerantut, the warning covers low-lying areas within a five-kilometre radius of the Sungai Pahang river basin, including Felda Jengka 24 (Block 11), Taman Ria, the Sungai Jan housing area, Felda Gelanggi 1 and 3, Kampung Baharu, Kampung Besul and Kampung Jerangsang.
“Other affected areas include Kampung Sungai Siam, Kampung Lata Kasah, Kampung Kuala Pengau, Kampung Kuala Teh, Kampung Batu Balai, Kampung Sempadan, Felda Sungai Retang, Felda Padang Piol and Kampung Paya Garuk,” the statement said.
Meanwhile, in Rompin, the warning covers low-lying areas within a five-kilometre radius of the Sungai Rompin river basin, including Kampung Aur, Kampung Meripoh, Kampung Tebu Hitam, Pantai Bernas, Kampung Ayau, Leban Chondong, Kampung Gading and Kampung Sarang Tiong.
The warning also extends to low-lying areas within a five-kilometre radius of the Sungai Pahang river basin, including Kampung Mikang, Kampung Buluh Nipis, Kampung Simpang Sepayang, Kampung Sepayang, Kampung Tebu Hitam, Kampung Tengah, Kampung Tekek, the Kampung Tekek low-cost housing area, Kampung Serinkin and Kampung Janglau 1, 2 and 3.
“Flooding may occur earlier or later than expected. The warning is issued to ensure that all residents, particularly those in areas at risk of flooding, remain vigilant and heed instructions from the authorities or flood disaster management agencies,” the statement said. — Bernama

Title: Pertak river surge: One body recovered, seven still missing in Kuala Kubu Bharu
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 10 — One of the eight individuals reported missing following a water surge at Sungai Pertak, Kuala Kubu Bharu, near here yesterday, was found drowned near the Pertak Bridge this morning.
Selangor Fire and Rescue Department (JBPM) assistant operations director, Asrul Riezal Asbar, said the victim, a local man identified as V. Vijayan was discovered about 2.7 kilometres from the spot where he was swept away at Lata Jebus.
“A total of 19 individuals, comprising four separate groups stranded in the area, were successfully rescued at 12.16am today,” he said when contacted.
Earlier, media reports indicated that during an incident at approximately 5.55pm yesterday, eight people consisting of one Yemeni national, one local, one Sri Lankan, one Nepalese, and four Indian nationals went missing after being swept away by the current.
He added that the search and rescue (SAR) operation resumed this morning, with the search area divided into four sectors around the incident site to locate the seven remaining missing individuals. — Bernama

Title: Anwar says SoftBank-led AI investment signals global confidence in Malaysia
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 10 — The SoftBank-led consortium’s investment in an artificial intelligence (AI) platform in Malaysia reflects global confidence in the country’s potential to develop and use AI, says Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim.
Anwar said the move also represents a significant milestone in the country’s digital transformation and supports Malaysia’s ambition to become an AI Nation by 2030, as outlined in the National AI Action Plan 2026-2030.
“I welcome the announcement by the SoftBank-led consortium, including Grab Holdings Ltd (Grab) and Petroleum Sarawak Bhd (Petros), to invest in an AI Infrastructure Platform in Sarawak and Peninsular Malaysia.
“The willingness of global investors like SoftBank and Masayoshi Son to invest in Malaysia reflects strong confidence in our national capabilities, investment climate and political stability,” he said in a post on X yesterday.
SoftBank chief executive officer Masayoshi Son reportedly selected Kuching, Sarawak, and Peninsular Malaysia for US$50 billion (RM202.86 billion) in AI infrastructure investments.
According to Anwar, combining SoftBank’s capital and expertise with Grab’s regional AI capabilities and proven track record of deploying AI across its ecosystem would significantly enhance Malaysia’s AI infrastructure and global competitiveness.
He said that as Malaysia develops its AI infrastructure, the country expects large-scale digital investments to support its sustainability goals. The project must also meet applicable federal and state requirements, including those relating to renewable energy use.
“I expect this investment to create skilled jobs for Malaysians and help more of our rakyat build expertise in AI.
“It should also create opportunities for our local businesses to supply goods and services as Malaysia builds its AI capabilities,” he said.
Anwar said the government would work with the relevant state authorities to facilitate the highly anticipated project. — Bernama

Title: Pertak river surge leaves eight missing, nine stranded in Kuala Kubu Bharu
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 10 — Eight people remain missing after they were swept away by swift currents, while nine others are reported to be stranded in three separate incidents involving different groups when the water level of Sungai Pertak surged in Kuala Kubu Bharu near here yesterday evening.
Selangor Fire and Rescue Department asst operations director Asrul Riezal Asbar the eight missing included an individual from a group of Yemeni nationals and locals, and seven from a group of 11 locals.
“For the first group, one was swept away and has yet to be found. Upstream, there are about 11 people. From the 11, seven were in the water and were swept away by currents,” he said when met by Bernama.
The nine stranded individuals included four that did not cross the river and five from another group reported to be stranded across the river.
Asrul Riezal said the department received a distress call at about 5.55pm and arrived at the scene at 6.30pm.
“We also received a call from the Orang Asli, who led the group… the search is still being continued. We have opened an incident control post to monitor water conditions and the surrounding areas to locate victims stranded at any location,” he added. — Bernama

Title: Melaka polls: 31 early voting centres open at 8am
Article:
MELAKA, Nov 10 — Thirty-one early polling centres for the 16th Melaka State Election opened at 8am today to allow 12,531 security personnel and their spouses to cast their ballots.
According to Election Commission (EC) statistics, the early voters comprise 9,769 military personnel and their spouses, and 2,762 police personnel.
All polling centres will close in stages according to the schedule set by the EC, namely at 12 noon, 2pm, and 5pm.
The state election is being held following the dissolution of the Melaka State Legislative Assembly on September 23, after receiving the consent of the Yang Dipertua Negeri of Melaka, Tun Mohd Ali Rustam.
The EC set today for early voting and November 14 for polling day.
Overall, 687,697 electors are eligible to vote in the state election.
The election sees Pakatan Harapan fielding candidates in 24 state seats, followed by Barisan Nasional (23), Parti Bersama Malaysia (16), Parti Pribumi Bersatu Malaysia (seven), Perikatan Nasional (five), Parti Pribumi Perkasa Malaysia (one), and three Independents.
In the 2021 Melaka State Election, Barisan Nasional won 21 seats to form the state government, while Pakatan Harapan won five seats and Perikatan Nasional two.
For the latest updates on the election, visit https://election.bernama.com/pm/melaka/2026/. — Bernama

Title: Instant torque, heavier batteries: What Malaysian motorists need to know before driving an EV
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 10 — Electric vehicles (EVs) may look and feel like conventional cars, but motorists switching to them need to get used to a different driving experience, from how quickly they accelerate to how they slow down when the accelerator is released.
Unlike petrol or diesel cars, which rely on an engine building up revolutions and changing gears to deliver power, EVs can produce strong torque from low speeds, allowing them to accelerate almost immediately.
While this makes EVs responsive and smooth to drive, the Malaysian Institute of Road Safety Research (Miros) said motorists unfamiliar with the technology could underestimate how quickly their vehicles pick up speed, particularly when pulling out of junctions, navigating roundabouts or manoeuvring in parking areas.
Miros research officer Mohd Firdaus Mohd Siam said instant torque was a normal characteristic of electric motors, but did not mean every EV was necessarily fast or difficult to control.
“Instant torque does not make every EV fast or hard to control, as performance depends on motor output, vehicle weight, gearing, traction, and drive mode.
“It is important to distinguish between torque, acceleration, and speed: torque is rotational force, acceleration is the change in velocity, and speed is how fast the vehicle moves. Acceleration is shaped by tyre grip, vehicle mass, and driver input, not torque alone,” he said.
Why does an EV accelerate differently from an ICE vehicle?
In a conventional internal combustion engine (ICE) vehicle, power delivery is tied to engine revolutions and gearbox response, whereas an electric motor can deliver torque from very low speeds.
This means motorists may experience a more immediate response when pressing the accelerator, particularly when moving away from traffic lights or joining faster-moving traffic.
Firdaus said new EV users could sometimes press the accelerator more than intended, resulting in sharper take-offs and leaving them less time and distance to react to hazards.
“Rapid acceleration reduces the time and distance available to detect hazards and respond, while aggressive throttle use on bends or wet roads can exceed tyre traction and trigger wheel slip or stability control.
“Over-application of the accelerator should not be confused with pressing the wrong pedal, and current evidence does not show EVs have higher crash rates than conventional cars,” he said.
He advised new owners to familiarise themselves with their vehicles, practise smooth starts and stops in low-traffic areas and initially use Normal or Eco driving modes rather than Sport mode.
Prof Zambri Harun, a professor of fluid mechanics at Universiti Kebangsaan Malaysia's Department of Mechanical and Manufacturing Engineering, Faculty of Engineering and Built Environment, said EV drivers could also improve battery efficiency by avoiding unnecessary acceleration and deceleration.
“EV users tend not to apply the brakes unnecessarily, and similarly not to accelerate aggressively, because of the regenerative braking system most vehicles have.
“The more one drives with unnecessary accelerations and decelerations, the faster the battery is exhausted,” he said.
Are EVs more difficult to stop because they are heavier?
Another difference motorists should understand is vehicle weight, as EV battery packs often make them heavier than comparable petrol or diesel models.
The additional mass means more energy is involved when a vehicle is moving, and greater force is required to bring it to a stop.
However, Firdaus said motorists should not automatically assume that heavier EVs have longer stopping distances or perform worse than conventional cars.
“Extra weight matters for braking and handling, but it does not automatically mean that EVs stop more slowly or perform worse in wet conditions.
“Stopping distance depends on many factors, including tyre grip, brake design, and electronic controls, not just vehicle mass,” he said.
He said heavier vehicles placed greater demands on brakes and tyres, making proper maintenance particularly important.
Prof Law Teik Hua, director of the Road Safety Research Center (RSRC) at Universiti Putra Malaysia, similarly said modern braking systems were designed to accommodate the additional mass of EVs, although motorists should still maintain sufficient distance from vehicles ahead.
“Heavier EVs require stronger force to decelerate to a standstill relative to their lighter counterparts travelling at comparable velocities.
“Stopping distances depend on multiple variables, including speed, tyre condition, road surface quality, braking system efficacy, and driver reaction times,” he said.
Law said stopping distances increased significantly at higher speeds, making early braking and cautious speed management important.
He also pointed out that EV batteries were often mounted low in the vehicle, lowering its centre of gravity and potentially reducing body roll during cornering.
However, this does not eliminate the need for careful driving, as tyre grip, suspension and road conditions continue to determine how well a vehicle handles.
What happens when you release the accelerator?
One feature that can take some getting used to is regenerative braking, which allows an EV to recover some of its kinetic energy when slowing down.
In conventional cars, braking generally relies on friction between the brake pads and discs to slow the wheels, converting the vehicle's kinetic energy into heat.
In an EV, the electric motor can act as a generator during deceleration, converting some of the vehicle's movement into electricity that is returned to the battery.
Depending on the model and settings, motorists may notice the vehicle slowing down when they lift their foot off the accelerator, a feature commonly associated with one-pedal driving.
Firdaus said regenerative braking did not replace conventional friction brakes, which remained essential for stronger deceleration and emergency stops.
“In many models, the system blends both types automatically when the driver presses the brake pedal. How much slowing happens when the accelerator is released depends on the vehicle and its settings.
“Some EVs offer adjustable regeneration or one-pedal driving, where the accelerator controls both speeding up and slowing down. This feature is not universal, and drivers should check the owner’s manual to understand how their car behaves,” he said.
He cautioned that regenerative braking could also vary depending on the battery's state of charge, temperature and system limitations, meaning drivers should not assume the vehicle would always slow down at the same rate.
For emergency situations, motorists should press the brake pedal firmly rather than rely on regenerative braking alone.
What should EV drivers know about driving in the rain?
Malaysia's frequent rainfall presents another challenge, particularly when motorists are unfamiliar with how their vehicles respond to slippery roads.
Firdaus said rain reduced tyre grip and visibility, while standing water could cause aquaplaning, where tyres lose contact with the road surface.
He said stopping distances in wet conditions could be double those on dry roads, regardless of whether the vehicle was electric or petrol-powered.
“Drivers should slow down before bends, avoid sudden steering or braking, and leave extra space between vehicles.
“Systems like ABS and stability control help, but they cannot overcome the limits of tyre grip,” he said.
Law similarly advised motorists to extend following distances, use gentle acceleration and avoid abrupt manoeuvres, particularly when overtaking or changing lanes in heavy rain.
He also stressed the importance of keeping tyres properly inflated and ensuring they had sufficient tread depth.
Both experts advised motorists against driving through flooded areas of unknown depth, as water immersion could pose risks to vehicle occupants and electrical components.
What should first-time EV drivers do before hitting the road?
For motorists switching from conventional cars, Firdaus said the first step should be to understand the vehicle's controls and obtain a proper handover from the dealer.
This includes learning how to operate the gear selector, parking brake, accelerator modes, regenerative braking settings, dashboard warnings and charging controls.
Miros' Safety Guide for Road Users and Public Concerning Electrified Vehicle Incident Management (MyEVIM) also recommends that owners receive a vehicle safety briefing and product familiarisation from an authorised dealer.
Firdaus advised motorists to begin with gentle acceleration and braking in a safe area before entering busy traffic, while paying particular attention to how their vehicles respond when the accelerator is released.
He also urged EV owners to check tyre pressures, tread depth and any visible damage, while ensuring tyres had the correct size, load and speed ratings.
Another consideration is that EVs are quieter at low speeds, meaning motorists should remain alert to pedestrians, cyclists and motorcyclists who may not hear an approaching vehicle.
Owners should also keep factory-fitted pedestrian alert systems active and avoid relying too heavily on driver-assistance features such as adaptive cruise control and lane support.
Practical precautions for new EV drivers
Safe driving depends on the driver's skills, the condition of the vehicle, the road environment and proper use of technology. MyEVIM guidance stresses that drivers should combine defensive driving habits with an understanding of their EV's specific features.
Before entering traffic, drivers should read the owner's manual and request a proper handover from the dealer. They should also understand the vehicle's charging requirements and use appropriate charging equipment installed by qualified professionals.
Tyres should be checked regularly for pressure, tread depth and damage, with motorists following the manufacturer's recommended specifications. Brakes, lights, wipers and stability or traction-control systems should also be maintained according to service schedules.
Driver-assistance features such as adaptive cruise control and lane support should be treated as aids rather than substitutes for attentive driving, while distractions such as mobile phone use should be avoided.
If an incident occurs, drivers should move occupants to safety, avoid high-voltage components and call 999, clearly identifying the vehicle as an EV. MyEVIM provides specific emergency guidance that should be followed alongside instructions from emergency responders.

Title: Malaysians still feel prices are high despite easing inflation, Bank Negara explains why
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 10 — While Malaysia’s inflation rate has moderated, the easing trend does not necessarily translate into a lower cost of living for households, highlighting the difference between changes in consumer prices and the actual affordability of everyday necessities.
The Consumer Price Index (CPI), the country’s primary measure of inflation, tracks the average change in prices of a representative basket of goods and services. However, it does not necessarily capture the different spending patterns, income levels and financial commitments of individual households.
This may be why Malaysians still feel financially stretched even when official inflation figures indicate that price increases are slowing.
In its article “Beyond the Headline: Inflation through the Eyes of Households”, published in its Annual Report 2025 earlier this year, Bank BNM explained that inflation measures the rate at which prices increase, rather than how high prices have already become.
It said Malaysia’s headline inflation averaged 1.4 per cent in 2025, its lowest level in five years, but the central bank acknowledged that the high cost of living remained a major concern for many households.
Inflation averaged 1.8 per cent in the first nine months of 2026, with core inflation at 2 per cent.
BNM said the difference is partly attributed to the way households experience price changes, particularly through frequently purchased items such as food and beverages, which tend to have a stronger influence on their perception of inflation.
It cited two behavioural factors influencing household perceptions, namely frequency bias, where staple foods and beverages are regularly purchased and carry greater weight in people’s assessments of price changes.
To better reflect this experience, economists use indicators such as the Everyday Price Index (EPI), which assigns greater weight to frequently purchased items in the CPI.
By emphasising these regular purchases, BNM said the EPI captures price changes that more closely mirror households’ day-to-day experiences.
It said household perceptions are also shaped by how people remember price changes.
“Price increases tend to leave a stronger and more lasting impression than price declines, even when both occur. This behavioural pattern, known as memory bias, is captured in the Perceived Price Index (PePI).”
The PePI is similar to the EPI but includes only items that have recorded price increases, while excluding those that have fallen in price. As a result, the PePI often shows a higher inflation rate than both the CPI and the EPI, reflecting the stronger impression that price hikes leave on households.
Purchasing power the real issue
The central bank said that beyond measuring inflation, the more fundamental issue is whether household incomes are growing enough to keep pace with the cumulative increase in prices.
Analysis by BNM showed that between 2019 and 2024, Malaysia’s headline CPI rose 9.3 per cent, while nominal wages per worker grew by only 7.2 per cent.
“In other words, this means that the average person must work more hours to afford the same basket of goods. This is clearly illustrated in the case of food. As prices rose faster than wages in recent years, households must now work longer just to meet their usual food expenses,” it said.
As the central bank, one of BNM’s key objectives is to ensure low and stable inflation.
“This is important as stable and predictable prices allow households and businesses to better plan their spending, saving and investment decisions. In turn, this helps to support economic activity and growth.
“Preserving household purchasing power, however, depends not only on prices but also on incomes; namely, when price increases are slow and predictable, households can maintain their purchasing power as long as wages rise alongside prices,” it elaborated.
In such conditions, BNM said steady inflation allows incomes time to adjust, helping households cope with higher prices and plan their spending with greater confidence.
It said recent income measures, such as revisions to the minimum wage, have helped to ease the burden on more than five million workers in Malaysia. Over the longer term, however, deeper structural reforms are needed to address the root causes of subdued wage growth in Malaysia.
“First, there is a need to create more high-skilled and high-paying jobs. In 2025, high-skilled jobs made up only 26 per cent of new positions, lower than the 5-year (2020–2024) average of 30 per cent,” it said.
BNM said this reflects the need to accelerate Malaysia’s transition towards higher value-added industries, strengthen technology adoption and increase investment in research and development to generate better-paying employment opportunities.
In this vein, initiatives such as the National Industrial Masterplan (NIMP2030) and the National Investment Aspirations (NIA) aim to attract higher-quality investments, promote technology-intensive production and generate more high-skilled jobs.
Beyond inflation control
While maintaining low and stable inflation remains important, addressing the cost-of-living challenge requires a broader policy response that tackles both household expenditure and income growth, it said.
“Monetary policy alone cannot fully preserve purchasing power, as households’ wellbeing is also shaped by wage growth, productivity and broader cost of living trends.”
“Even with moderate inflation, many households continue to grapple with higher living costs amid slow wage growth,” said the central bank.
BNM said income growth needs to outpace price increases to secure better living standards and strengthen purchasing power.
It added that when expenses rise faster than incomes, even small price increases can feel significant to households, shaping how affordable things seem and how they view the broader economy.
“Ultimately, strengthening households’ purchasing power requires a holistic and coordinated policy strategy,” it said.
The government’s efforts to raise wages, including the recent increase in the minimum wage to RM2,000 in the Budget 2027 from RM1,700, provide some relief to workers. However, sustained improvements in living standards would depend on broader wage and productivity growth.
The new minimum wage is set to take effect in June 2027 and will benefit more than four million workers.
In its report, BNM said this entails complementing monetary policy with targeted fiscal support for vulnerable groups and implementing structural reforms that boost incomes and productivity.
In Budget 2027, Sumbangan Asas Rahmah (SARA) aid has been extended to nearly 13 million Malaysians, including the M40 group.
As of October 22, RM3.6 billion had been disbursed to Sumbangan Tunai Rahmah (STR) cash aid recipients through three payment phases. In total, nearly RM12 billion in STR and SARA assistance had been channelled to eligible recipients.
The allocation for STR and SARA would be increased to RM16 billion in 2027, with monthly SARA assistance raised to RM150, or RM1,800 annually.
“By tackling both price and wage dynamics, policymakers can safeguard purchasing power and support sustainable economic growth over the long term,” said BNM.
Hence, while a lower inflation rate may indicate that price increases are becoming more manageable, the central bank added that meaningful improvements in living standards will only be felt when household incomes grow sufficiently to restore and strengthen purchasing power. — Bernama

Title: Can Malaysia turn monsoon floods into drought-proof water reserves instead?
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 10 — The overflow of rainwater, which poses a risk of causing flood disasters during the monsoon season, can actually become a lifesaver in facing the threat of the dry season, thereby ensuring the continuity of domestic supply and national food security.
Therefore, the main challenge now is to what extent some of the water overflow during the North-east Monsoon (MTL) can be harvested, stored, and reused optimally during hot weather to reduce pressure on the water supply system and the agricultural sector.
On November 1, Bernama reported that Malaysia could face two opposing weather challenges in the coming months, starting with the threat of floods due to the MTL before possibly being hit by drought following the Super El Nino phenomenon in 2027, which could affect water supply and the agri-food sector.
Universiti Malaysia Perlis (UniMAP) water resource expert Associate Professor Dr Zulkarnain Hassan said Malaysia needs to emphasise efforts to maximise rainwater harvesting, especially in areas receiving heavy rainfall such as the East Coast of Peninsular Malaysia, as well as Sabah and Sarawak.
He explained that although dams and reservoirs usually reach maximum capacity during the monsoon, the potential to store excess water needs to be translated into more concrete actions before the country enters the drought phase.
Zulkarnain, who is also a hydrology expert, said that among the approaches that can be expanded is the utilisation of ponds, lakes, and former mining areas as alternative catchment areas through the Riverbank Water Storage (TAPS) method, similar to the implementation of the Raw Water Guarantee Scheme (SJAM) in Selangor.
He said the initiative is capable of providing a backup water reserve for two to three months during droughts or when water treatment plants halt operations due to pollution, and it should be explored in other states according to local geographical suitability.
Touching on dam management, Zulkarnain said the main challenge is optimising the operation of multi-purpose dams, particularly in balancing the need to release water to reduce flood risk without compromising the dry season storage reserves.
For example, he said the Bukit Merah Dam in Perak not only serves to supply water for irrigation and domestic use but also functions as flood control infrastructure and a recreational zone.
“This challenge is more pronounced when the operation of dam water release in Malaysia is still largely managed manually and relies on the operator’s experience. This situation risks causing excessive water release solely due to safety and flood control factors,” he told Bernama.
In this regard, he proposed the expansion of the Decision Support System (DSS) using smart weather forecasting technology to help operators determine the precise quantity of water release based on reservoir levels and current needs.
In addition, Zulkarnain said emphasised the need to reduce the Non-Revenue Water (NRW) rate through the replacement of old pipes, rapid leak detection, and more efficient distribution pressure management.
He also suggested that the community cultivate the practice of collecting rainwater for non-drinking purposes such as watering plants and washing vehicles, in addition to recommending the “Sponge City” concept in urban planning to absorb excess rainwater to reduce flash floods and increase groundwater reserves.
Meanwhile, agricultural technology expert from Universiti Putra Malaysia (UPM), Dr Wan Fazilah Fazlil Ilahi believes that the overflow of MTL water should be seen as a valuable asset to ensure that agricultural activities can continue sustainably during the dry season.
She said that the approach to farm water management needs to shift from merely draining water away during heavy rain to efforts to collect, store, and recycle the resource for irrigation.
She said that runoff water from farmland areas, agricultural structure roofs, and drainage systems can be channelled directly into farm retention ponds or rainwater harvesting tanks, especially in rural agricultural areas lacking large-scale irrigation systems.
“Vegetable farms can combine rainwater harvesting tanks with drip irrigation systems, while fruit farms can use retention ponds as a water source during the dry season,” she said.
She said the measure is important considering that crops such as chilies, tomatoes, cucumbers, and leafy vegetables are at risk of root damage and diseases when water stagnates for too long, while rice, corn, fruits, and certain commodity crops can be affected by prolonged water shortages.
That situation, she said, could affect crop yields and quality, increase production costs, and put pressure on farmers’ incomes, especially smallholders with limited financial capacity.
Wan Fazilah said that the use of drip irrigation systems can save water between 20 and 40 per cent, while the Alternate Wetting and Drying (AWD) method for padi cultivation can save around 15 to 30 per cent of water usage.
According to her, the technology does not require high costs because small farmers can implement it modularly through basic tanks and pipes, in addition to recommending irrigation practices.
“We should not wait until a drought hits before we want to take action. The MTL period is the best opportunity to strengthen infrastructure and water storage systems in preparation for the possibility of water shortages in the future,” she added. — Bernama
